mechanist:infusions::Enhanced Weapon.text: Item: A simple or martial weapon

mechanist:infusions::Exomuscular Armor.text: Item: A suit of armor (requires installation)

mechanist:infusions::Hardlight Rounds.text: Item: A simple or martial weapon with the ammunition property (requires installation)

mechanist:infusions::Replicate High-End.text: Using this infusion, you replicate a particular high-end item. You can learn this infusion multiple times; each time you do so, choose a high-end item that you can make with it, picking from the Replicable Items tables. A table's title tells you the level you must be in the class to choose an item from the table. Alternatively, you can choose the high-end item from among the common high-end items in the game, not including potions or scrolls.

mechanist:infusions::Returning Weapon.text: Item: A civilian or military weapon with the thrown property

mechanist:infusions::Synaptic Lining.text: Item: A suit of armor or robes

mechanist:infusions::Utility Droid.text: Item: A gem or crystal worth at least $10,000 gp

mechanist:mech-pilot::Pilot's Kit.text: When you adopt this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with two land vehicles of your choice.

mechanist:mech-pilot::Mech Pilot Tech.text: You always have certain tech prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Mech Pilot Tech table. These techs count as mechanist techs for you, but they don’t count against the number of mechanist techs you prepare.

mechanist:mech-pilot::Call Mech.text: At 3rd level, the pilot can summon their mech to them as an action. If the mech is within 300 feet to its pilot, it will try its best to reach its pilot within three turns. If the distance is greater than one mile, then the mech will take anywhere from five to ten minutes to reach its pilot.

mechanist:mech-pilot::Combat Modificatio.text: Starting at 5th level, the Mechanist gains the Extra Attack feature while within their Mech.

mechanist:mech-pilot::Greater Weapon Int.text: At 9th level, the Mechanist can integrate a third attachment into their Mech. Further, the Mechanist can swap one attachment during any short rest. Furthermore, the Mechanist can now use their Tinker feature on their Suit, applying a single infusion to it.

mechanist:mech-pilot::Spinal Attachment.text: At 15th level, the Mech can be fitted with a powerful attachment onto the suit. Each model has its own attachment. Each attachment can be used once and is refilled at the end of a long rest.

ordinator::Techcasting.text: As a conduit for divine power, you can cast Ordinator Techs. See Techs Rules for the general rules of Techcasting and the Techs Listing for the Ordinator Tech list.

ordinator::Cerebral Synergy.text: At 1st level, you choose a Cerebral Synergy shaped by your AI's personality. Your choice grants you Synergy Techs and other features when you choose it at 1st level. It also grants you additional ways to use AI Assistance when you gain that feature at 2nd level, and additional benefits at 6th, 8th, and 17th levels.

ordinator::Synergy Techs.text: Each Synergy has a list of Techs—its Synergy Techs—that you gain at the Ordinator levels noted in the Synergy description. Once you gain a Synergy Tech, you always have it prepared, and it doesn’t count against the number of Techs you can prepare each day.

ordinator::AI Assistance.text: At 2nd level, you gain the ability to have your A.I assist you in combat, using that energy to fuel technical effects. You start with two such effects: Turn Hacked and an effect determined by your Law. Some Laws grant you additional effects as you advance in levels, as noted in the Law description.

ordinator::AI Assistance: Turn Hacked.text: As an action, your AI inhibits and scrambles Hacked enemy code, censuring the Hacked. Each Hacked that can see or hear you within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw. If the creature fails its saving throw, it is turned for 1 minute or until it takes any damage.

ordinator::Ability Score Improvement.text: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

ordinator::Destroy Hacked.text: Starting at 5th level, when a Hacked fails its saving throw against your Turn Hacked feature, the creature is instantly destroyed if its challenge rating is at or below a certain threshold, as shown in the Destroy Hacked table.

ordinator::Symbiotic Intervention.text: Beginning at 10th level, you can call on your AI’s inherent power to intervene on your behalf when your need is great.

ordinator::Cerebral Synergies.text: The A.I companions of Ordinators have personalities and goals of their own, be it a desire to aid humanity through healing and medical technology, aiding the Ordinator in tricks and pranks, or assisting them in targeted, ferocious strikes. AIs frequently choose their Ordinator host based on complementary personalities; a ferocious, fight focused Ordinator could have an equally aggressive AI, while a gentler, more supportive Ordinator could have a soothing, shy AI.

ordinator:archivist::Bookworm.text: At 1st level, you learn two languages of your choice. You also become proficient in your choice of two of the following skills: Tech, History, Nature, or Culture.

ordinator:archivist::A.I Assistance: Wik.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your A.I Assistance to tap into a search engine for online archives of knowledge. As an action, you choose one skill or tool. For 10 minutes, you have proficiency with the chosen skill or tool.

ordinator:archivist::A.I Assistance: BIO.text: At 6th level, you can use your A.I Assistance to scan a creature's thoughts. You can then use your access to the creature's mind to command it.

ordinator:archivist::Potent Techcasting.text: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric Trick.

ordinator:archivist::Holographic Recreat.text: Starting at 17th level, you can digitally reconstruct events of the past that relate to an object you hold or your immediate surroundings. You spend at least 1 minute searching and scanning through your archive, then create holographic reconstructions of recent events. You can use this feature for a number of minutes equal to your Wisdom score and must maintain concentration during that time, as if you were casting a Tech. Your allies can observe this holographic recreation.

ordinator:city::Bonus Trick.text: When you choose this synergy at 1st level, you gain the on/off trick in addition to your chosen tricks.

ordinator:city::Bonus Proficiencies.text: Also starting at 1st level, you gain proficiency with civilian and military ranged weapons, and proficiency with vehicles (land).

ordinator:city::Heart of the City.text: From 1st level, you are able to tap into the spirit of community found in the city. While you are within any city, you can gain advantage on a single Charisma (Deception, Intimidation or Persuasion) check, and are considered proficient in the appropriate skill. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1). You regain any expended uses when you finish a long rest.

ordinator:city::A.I. Assistance: Whisper.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can ask your A.I. for assistance to reach out to the city's remaining fragments of memory for aid. As an action, you can reach out to the city, and any city utility within 30 feet of you either works perfectly or shuts down entirely for 1 minute (your choice).

ordinator:city::Block Watch.text: Starting at 6th level, your awareness while in the city extends preternaturally. While in an urban environment, you are considered proficient in the Insight and Perception skills, and you add double your proficiency bonus to Wisdom (Insight) and Wisdom (Perception) checks, instead of your normal proficiency bonus.

ordinator:city::Power of the City.text: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with energy drawn from the very essence of the city's thoughts. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 software damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra software damage increases to 2d8.

ordinator:city::Express Transit.text: At 17th level, you can use mass transit route to transport instantaneously to other points in the city. Starting from a bus stop, train station, subway stop or other suitable mass transit site within the city, you can teleport to any other similar transit stop within the city, as if you had cast a transmit tech whose destination is a permanent transmission beacon you know. Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before using it again.

ordinator:grim::Bonus Proficiency.text: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with military weapons.

ordinator:grim::Reaper.text: At 1st level, you learn one Biochemistry Trick of your choice from any Tech list. When you cast a Biochemistry Trick that normally targets only one creature, the Tech can instead target two creatures within range and within 5 feet of each other.

ordinator:grim::A.I Assistance: Touch of.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use A.I Assistance to destroy another creature's life force by touch. When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can use A.I Assistance to deal extra entropic damage to the target. The damage equals 5 + twice your Ordinator level.

ordinator:grim::The Call of The Void.text: Starting at 6th level, your ability to channel negative energy becomes more potent. Entropic damage dealt by your Ordinator Techs and A.I Assistance options ignores resistance to entropic damage.

ordinator:grim::Entropic Strike.text: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with entropic energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an a 1d8 entropic damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

ordinator:grim::Improved Reaper.text: Starting at 17th level, when you cast a Biochemistry Tech of 1st through 5th level that targets only one creature, the Tech can instead target two creatures within range and within 5 feet of each other. If the Tech consumes its material components, you must provide them for each target.

ordinator:guarantor::Insurance Policy.text: At 1st level, you gain the ability to manipulate the line between life and death. When you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a Tech to a creature at 0 hit points, you instead use the highest number possible for each die.

ordinator:guarantor::Hacked Tracker.text: At 1st level, you gain the ability to occasionally sense the presence of the Hacked, whose existence is an insult to the natural cycle of life. As an action, you scan your surroundings to detect Hacked. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any Hacked within 60 feet of you that isn't behind total cover and that isn't protected from Observation tech. This sense doesn't tell you anything about a creature's capabilities or identity.

ordinator:guarantor::A.I Assistance: Mar.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your A.I Assistance to mark another creature’s life force for termination.

ordinator:guarantor::Not Today.text: At 6th level, you gain the ability to impede death’s progress. As a reaction when you or an ally that you can see within 30 feet of you suffers a critical hit, you can turn that attack into a normal hit. Any effects triggered by a critical hit are canceled.

ordinator:guarantor::Potent Techcasting.text: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Ordinator Trick.

ordinator:guarantor::Stolen Sustain.text: At 17th level, when an enemy you can see dies within 30 feet of you, you or one ally of your choice that is within 30 feet of you regains hit points equal to the enemy’s number of Hit Dice. You can use this feature only if you aren't incapacitated. Once you use it, you can't do so again until the start of your next turn.

ordinator:industrialist::Bonus Proficien.text: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor and mechanic's tools.

ordinator:industrialist::Mechanical Mant.text: At 1st level, you gain the ability to temporarily upgrade a weapon or armor. At the end of a long rest, you can touch one nontechnical object that is a suit of armor or a simple or martial weapon. Until the end of your next long rest or until you die, the object becomes a high-end item, granting a +1 bonus to AC if it’s armor or a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls if it’s a weapon.

ordinator:industrialist::A.I Assistance:.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your A.I Assistance to create simple items.

ordinator:industrialist::Scorched Strong.text: Starting at 6th level, your mastery of the forge grants you special abilities:

ordinator:industrialist::Gasoline Strike.text: At 8th level, you gain the ability to douse your weapon strikes with burning petroleum. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 fire damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

ordinator:industrialist::Burning Hot.text: At 17th level, your affinity with fire and metal becomes more powerful:

ordinator:lifegiver::Bonus Proficiency.text: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor.

ordinator:lifegiver::Damn Good Doctor.text: Also starting at 1st level, your healing Techs are more effective. Whenever you use a Tech of 1st level or higher to restore hit points to a creature, the creature regains additional hit points equal to 2 + the Tech's level.

ordinator:lifegiver::A.I Assistance: Hea.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your A.I Assistance to heal the badly injured.

ordinator:lifegiver::Pill Popper.text: Beginning at 6th level, the healing Techs you cast on others heal you as well. When you cast a Tech of 1st level or higher that restores hit points to a creature other than you, you regain hit points equal to 2 + the Tech's level.

ordinator:lifegiver::Neon Strike.text: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with incredible energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 neon damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

ordinator:lifegiver::Chief of Medicine.text: Starting at 17th level, when you would normally roll one or more dice to restore hit points with a Tech, you instead use the highest number possible for each die. For example, instead of restoring 2d6 hit points to a creature, you restore 12.

ordinator:order::Bonus Proficiencies.text: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency with heavy armor. You also gain proficiency in the Intimidation or Persuasion skill (your choice).

ordinator:order::Points of Authority.text: Starting at 1st level, you can embolden an ally to attack with clockwork timing. If you cast a tech with a tech slot of 1st level or higher and target an ally with the tech, that ally can use their reaction immediately after the tech to make one weapon attack against a creature of your choice that you can see.

ordinator:order::A.I. Assistance: Hierar.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your A.I. Assistance to exert an overpowering presence toward others.

ordinator:order::Obsessive Compulsion.text: At 6th level, you become remarkably adept at utilizing techs that compel others.

ordinator:order::Overbearing Strike.text: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with mind-searing energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 software damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

ordinator:order::Marked for Destruction.text: Starting at 17th level, enemies you designate for destruction wilt under the combined efforts of you and your allies. If you deal your Overbearing Strike damage to a creature on your turn, you can mark that creature until the start of your next turn. The next time one of your allies hits the marked creature with an attack, the target also takes 2d8 software damage, and the mark ends. You can mark a creature in this way only once per turn.

ordinator:peacebringer::Trained Diplomat.text: When you choose this synergy at 1st level, you gain proficiency in the Insight, Performance, or Persuasion skill (your choice).

ordinator:peacebringer::Unitary Bond.text: Starting at 1st level, you can forge an empowering bond among people who are at peace with one another. As an action, you choose a number of willing creatures within 30 feet of you (this can include yourself) equal to your proficiency bonus. You create a technological bond among them for 10 minutes or until you use this feature again. While any bonded creature is within 30 feet of another, the creature can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw it makes. Each creature can add the d4 no more than once per turn.

ordinator:peacebringer::A.I. Assistance:.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your A.I. Assistance to make your very presence a soothing balm. As an action, you can move up to your speed, without provoking opportunity attacks, and when you move within 5 feet of any other creature during this action, you can restore a number of hit points to that creature equal to 2d6 + your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1 hit point). A creature can receive this healing only once whenever you take this action.

ordinator:peacebringer::Protective Bond.text: Beginning at 6th level, the bond you forge between people helps them protect each other. When a creature affected by your Unitary Bond feature is about to take damage, a second bonded creature within 30 feet of the first can use its reaction to teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the first creature. The second creature then takes all the damage instead.

ordinator:peacebringer::Potent Techs.text: At 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any ordinator trick.

ordinator:peacebringer::Expansive Bond.text: At 17th level, the benefits of your Unitary Bond and Protective Bond features now work when the creatures are within 60 feet of each other. Moreover, when a creature uses Protective Bond to take someone else’s damage, the creature has resistance to that damage.

ordinator:promethean::Bonus Trick.text: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain the light transfer Trick if you don't already know it.

ordinator:promethean::Blinding Flash.text: Also at 1st level, you can interpose a bright light between yourself and an attacking enemy. When you are attacked by a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll, causing light to flare before the attacker before it hits or misses. An attacker that can't be blinded is immune to this feature.

ordinator:promethean::A.I Assistance: Di.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your A.I Assistance to harness neon light, banishing darkness and dealing Neon damage to your foes.

ordinator:promethean::Improved Blinding.text: Starting at 6th level, you can also use your Blinding Flash feature when a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you attacks a creature other than you.

ordinator:promethean::Potent Techcasting.text: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any cleric Trick.

ordinator:promethean::Shining Bright.text: Starting at 17th level, you can use your action to activate an aura of light that lasts for 1 minute or until you dismiss it using another action. You emit bright light in a 60-foot radius and dim light 30 feet beyond that. Your enemies in the bright light have disadvantage on saving throws against any Tech that deals fire or Neon damage.

ordinator:sanguine::Bonus Proficiency.text: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with military weapons.

ordinator:sanguine::Bioreaction Beacon.text: From 1st level, your AI utilizes all available biomass and mysdata, even from those of the wounds you inflicted, to fuel your techs. When you use a tech of 1st level or higher to inflict damage to any bio-harvestable creature, those creatures suffer additional entropic damage equal to 2 + the tech's level.

ordinator:sanguine::AI Assistance: Vesse.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your AI Assistance to briefly commandeer a creature's circulatory and fuel line systems.

ordinator:sanguine::AI Assistance: Trans.text: Starting at 6th level, you can use your AI Assistance to catalogue a sample of vital fluid or biomass from a bio-harvestable creature that is at least 2 ounces, and that has been spilled or separated no longer than a week ago.

ordinator:sanguine::Biochemical Manufact.text: At 8th level, you can synthesize your own vital fluid into nanite-enhancing chemical compounds to recover tech slots. As an action, you can recover tech slots that have a combined level equal to or less than half of your ordinator level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. You immediately reduce your hit points by 1d6 per tech slot level recovered. You can’t use this feature again until you finish a long rest

ordinator:sanguine::Conscripted Organ Do.text: At 17th level, as an action, you can transmit a hemomagnetic nanite command that extends 30 feet out from you. This aura siphons the nanites and biomass of nearby foes, causing them to deteriorate, malfunction, and hemorrhage.

ordinator:shadowdancer::Bonus Proficienc.text: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with military weapons and heavy armor.

ordinator:shadowdancer::Night Vision.text: Starting at 1st level, you can see through the deepest gloom. You have darkvision out to a range of 300 feet. In that radius, you can see in dim light as if it were bright light and in darkness as if it were dim light.

ordinator:shadowdancer::Vigilance Subrou.text: At 1st level, your ability to split your consciousness between your own mind and that of your A.I. synergy can grant greater vigilance. As an action, you give one creature you touch (including possibly yourself) advantage on the next initiative roll the creature makes. This benefit ends immediately after the roll or if you use this feature again.

ordinator:shadowdancer::A.I. Assistance:.text: At 2nd level, you can use your A.I. Assistance to refresh your allies with soothing energies.

ordinator:shadowdancer::Hovertech.text: Starting at 6th level, you can draw on liminal energies to rise into the air. As a bonus action when you are in dim light or darkness, you can give yourself a flying speed equal to your walking speed for 1 minute. You can use this bonus action a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

ordinator:shadowdancer::Neon Strike.text: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with Neon energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 neon damage. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

ordinator:shadowdancer::Liminal Shroud.text: At 17th level, the liminality that you summon offers a protective aura: you and your allies have half cover while in the sphere created by your Liminal Sanctuary.

ordinator:stormrider::Bonus Proficiencie.text: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with military weapons and heavy armor.

ordinator:stormrider::Storm Rebuke.text: Also at 1st level, you can thunderously rebuke attackers. When a creature within 5 feet of you that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to cause the creature to make a Dexterity saving throw. The creature takes 2d8 lightning or thunder damage (your choice) on a failed saving throw, and half as much damage on a successful one.

ordinator:stormrider::A.I. Assistance: D.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your A.I. Assistance to wield the power of the storm with unchecked ferocity.

ordinator:stormrider::Concussive Strike.text: At 6th level, when you deal lightning or thunder damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can also push it up to 10 feet away from you.

ordinator:stormrider::Storm Strike.text: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with surges of storm-like energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 lightning or thunder damage to the target (your choice). When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

ordinator:stormrider::Stormborn.text: At 17th level, you have a flying speed equal to your current walking speed whenever you are not underground or indoors.

ordinator:techie::Digital Initiate.text: When you choose this domain at 1st level, you gain proficiency in the Tech skill, and you gain two Tricks of your choice from the Techwizard Tech list. For you, these Tricks count as Ordinator Tricks.

ordinator:techie::A.I Assistance: Digita.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your A.I Assistance to abjure digital creatures.

ordinator:techie::Virus Breaker.text: Starting at 6th level, when you restore hit points to an ally with a Tech of 1st level or higher, you can also end one Tech of your choice on that creature. The level of the Tech you end must be equal to or lower than the level of the Tech slot you use to cast the healing Tech.

ordinator:techie::Potent Techcasting.text: Starting at 8th level, you add your Wisdom modifier to the damage you deal with any Ordinator Trick.

ordinator:techie::Digital Mastery.text: At 17th level, you choose four Techs from the Techwizard Tech list, one from each of the following levels: 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th. You add them to your list of domain Techs. Like your other domain Techs, they are always prepared and count as Ordinator Techs for you.

ordinator:trickster::Duplicitous Trainin.text: When you choose this synergy at 1st level, you gain proficiency in the Deception or Stealth skill (your choice).

ordinator:trickster::Stealth Module.text: Starting when you choose this synergy at 1st level, you can use your action to touch a willing creature other than yourself to give it advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. This Buffing lasts for 1 hour or until you use this feature again.

ordinator:trickster::A.I. Assistance: In.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your A.I. Assistance to create an illusory duplicate of yourself.

ordinator:trickster::A.I. Assistance: Di.text: Starting at 6th level, you can use your A.I. Assistance to vanish. As an action, you become invisible until the end of your next turn. You become visible if you attack or cast a tech.

ordinator:trickster::Insidious Strike.text: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with lethal toxins. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 poison damage to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

ordinator:trickster::Improved Duplicity.text: At 17th level, you can create up to four duplicates of yourself, instead of one, when you use Invoke Duplicity. As a bonus action on your turn, you can move any number of them up to 30 feet, to a maximum range of 120 feet.

ordinator:warmonger::Trained for Violenc.text: At 1st level, you gain proficiency with military weapons and heavy armor.

ordinator:warmonger::Battle Ready.text: From 1st level, your A.I. companion can aid you in battle. When you use the Attack action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

ordinator:warmonger::A.I. Assistance: Gu.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your A.I. Assistance to strike with supernatural accuracy. When you make an attack roll, you can use your A.I. Assistance to gain a +10 bonus to the roll. You make this choice after you see the roll, but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

At 6th level, when a creature within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can use your reaction to grant that creature a +10 bonus to the roll, using your A.I. Assistance. You make this choice after you see the roll, but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.

ordinator:warmonger::Powerful Strike.text: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with additional power. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 damage of the same type dealt by the weapon to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

ordinator:warmonger::Battle Hardened.text: At 17th level, you gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nontechnical weapons.

ordinator:wastelander::Wasteland Trainin.text: At 1st level, you learn one trick of your choice from the shut-in tech list. You also gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, Nature, or Survival.

ordinator:wastelander::A.I. Assistance:.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your A.I. Assistance to charm animals and plants.

ordinator:wastelander::Elemental Dampeni.text: Starting at 6th level, when you or a creature within 30 feet of you takes acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder damage, you can use your reaction to grant resistance to the creature against that instance of the damage.

ordinator:wastelander::Surge Strike.text: At 8th level, you gain the ability to infuse your weapon strikes with surge energy. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 cold, fire, or lightning damage (your choice) to the target. When you reach 14th level, the extra damage increases to 2d8.

ordinator:wastelander::Nature Mastery.text: At 17th level, you gain the ability to command animals and plant creatures. While creatures are charmed by your Nature Protocol feature, you can take a bonus action on your turn to verbally command what each of those creatures will do on its next turn.

outlaw::Expertise.text: At 6th level, choose two more of your proficiencies (skill, tool, or vehicle). Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.

outlaw::Sneak Attack.text: Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe’s distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a finesse or a ranged weapon.

outlaw::Scumslang.text: During your time on the streets, you have learned scumslang—a constantly shifting mix of dialect, jargon, and code that allows you to hide messages in seemingly normal conversation. Only another creature that knows scumslang understands such messages. It takes four times longer to convey such a message than it does to speak the same idea plainly.

outlaw::Cunning Action.text: Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.

outlaw::Outlaw Archetype.text: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you emulate in the exercise of your outlaw abilities. Choose one of the Outlaw Archetypes presented at the end of this class. Your archetype choice grants you features at 3rd level and then again at 9th, 13th, and 17th level.

outlaw::Steady Aim.text: As a 3rd-level outlaw, you learn to steady yourself for precise attacks. As a bonus action, you can grant yourself advantage on the next attack roll you make during the current turn. You can only use this ability if you have not moved during the current turn. When you use this ability, your speed becomes 0 until the end of the current turn.

outlaw::Ability Score Improvement.text: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

outlaw::Uncanny Dodge.text: Starting at 5th level, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack’s damage against you.

outlaw::Evasion.text: Beginning at 7th level, you can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a kaiju’s atomic breath or the explosion from a grenade. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

outlaw::Reliable Talent.text: By 11th level, you have refined your chosen skills until they approach perfection. Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

outlaw::Blindsense.text: Starting at 14th level, if you are able to hear, you are aware of the location of any hidden or invisible creature within 10 feet of you.

outlaw::Slippery Mind.text: By 15th level, you have learned how to turn your sheer stubbornness into a potent mental defense. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.

outlaw::Elusive.text: Beginning at 18th level, you are so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll has advantage against you while you aren’t incapacitated.

outlaw::Devil’s Own Luck.text: At 20th level, you have an uncanny knack for succeeding when you need to. If your attack misses a target within range, you can turn the miss into a hit. Alternatively, if you fail an ability check, you can treat the d20 roll as a 20.

outlaw:assassin::Bonus Proficiencies.text: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with disguise kits and poison kits.

outlaw:assassin::Assassinate.text: Starting at 3rd level, you are at your deadliest when you get the drop on your enemies. You have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn’t taken a turn in the combat yet. In addition, any hit you score against a creature that is surprised is a critical hit.

outlaw:assassin::Infiltration Expertise.text: Starting at 9th level, you can unfailingly create false identities for yourself. You must spend your entire prep phase/downtime unit and $10,000 to establish the history, profession, and affiliations for an identity. You can’t establish an identity that belongs to someone else. For example, you might acquire appropriate clothing, ID cards, and official-looking certification to establish yourself as a member of a corp from a distant city so you can insinuate yourself into the company of other executives. This effectively grants you basic access (entryway through the front door, warehouse, shipping deck) but no further. This will also be DM’s discretion as to what officially classifies as "basic access".

outlaw:assassin::Impostor.text: At 13th level, you gain the ability to unerringly mimic another person’s speech, writing, and behavior. You must spend at least three hours studying these three components of the person’s behavior, listening to speech, examining handwriting, and observing mannerisms.

outlaw:assassin::Death Strike.text: Starting at 17th level, you become a master of instant death. When you attack and hit a creature that is surprised, it must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your Dexterity modifier + your proficiency bonus). On a failed save, double the damage of your attack against the creature.

outlaw:gambler::Gambling Savant.text: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, choose three games of chance or skill. You gain proficiency with those games, and you can choose to gain expertise with any of them when you would gain expertise.

outlaw:gambler::Ear for Deceit.text: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you develop a keen ear for picking out lies. Whenever you make a Wisdom (Insight) check to determine whether a creature is lying, treat a roll of 7 or lower on the d20 as an 8.

outlaw:gambler::Eye for Detail.text: Starting at 3rd level, you can use a bonus action to make a Wisdom (Perception) check to spot a hidden creature or object or to make an Intelligence (Investigation) check to uncover or decipher clues.

outlaw:gambler::Insightful Fighting.text: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to decipher an opponent’s tactics and develop a counter to them. As a bonus action, you make a Wisdom (Insight) check against a creature you can see that isn’t incapacitated, contested by the target’s Charisma (Deception) check. If you succeed, you can use your Sneak Attack against that target even if you don’t have advantage on the attack roll, but not if you have disadvantage on it.

outlaw:gambler::Steady Eye.text: At 9th level, you gain advantage on any Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Investigation) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

outlaw:gambler::Unerring Eye.text: At 13th level, your senses are almost impossible to foil. As an action, you sense the presence of holograms, shapechangers not in their original form, and other tech designed to deceive the senses within 30 feet of you, provided you aren’t blinded or deafened. You sense that an effect is attempting to trick you, but you gain no insight into what is hidden or into its true nature.

outlaw:gambler::Eye for Weakness.text: At 17th level, you learn to exploit a creature’s weaknesses by carefully studying its tactics and movement. While your Insightful Fighting feature applies to a creature, your Sneak Attack damage against that creature increases by 3d6.

outlaw:hacktivist::Techcasting.text: When you reach 3rd level, you augment your martial prowess with the ability to cast techs.

outlaw:hacktivist::Tricks.text: You learn three tricks: hovering helping hand and two other tricks of your choice from the techwizard tech list. You learn another techwizard trick of your choice at 10th level.

outlaw:hacktivist::Tech Slots.text: The Hacktivist Techcasting table shows how many tech slots you have to cast your techs of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these techs, you must expend a slot of the tech’s level or higher. You regain all expended tech slots when you finish a long rest.

outlaw:hacktivist::Techs Known of 1st Le.text: You know three 1st-level techwizard techs of your choice, two of which you must choose from the conception and deception schools on the techwizard tech list.

outlaw:hacktivist::Techcasting Ability.text: Intelligence is your techcasting ability for your techwizard techs, since you learn your techs through dedicated study and practical application. You use your Intelligence whenever a tech refers to your techcasting ability. In addition, you use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a techwizard tech you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

outlaw:hacktivist::Improved Helping Hand.text: Starting at 3rd level, when you cast helping hand, you can make the spectral hand invisible, and you can perform the following additional tasks with it:

outlaw:hacktivist::Tech Ambush.text: Starting at 9th level, if you are hidden from a creature when you cast a tech on it, the creature has disadvantage on any saving throw it makes against the tech this turn.

outlaw:hacktivist::Distracting Hand.text: At 13th level, you gain the ability to distract targets with your helping hand. As a bonus action on your turn, you can designate a creature within 5 feet of the invisible hand created by the tech. Doing so gives you advantage on attack rolls against that creature until the end of the turn.

outlaw:hacktivist::Tech Thief.text: At 17th level, you gain the ability to steal a tech from another techcaster by repurposing their peripherals, hacking their brain, or otherwise diverting control of the tech from them to you.

outlaw:investigator::Master of Intrigue.text: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with disguise kits, forgery kits, and one gaming set of your choice. You also learn two old world languages of your choice.

outlaw:investigator::Master of Tactics.text: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the Help action as a bonus action. Additionally, when you use the Help action to aid an ally in attacking a creature, the target of that attack can be within 30 feet of you, rather than 5 feet of you, if the target can see or hear you.

outlaw:investigator::Insightful Manipula.text: Starting at 9th level, if you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own. The DM tells you if the creature is your equal, superior, or inferior in regard to two of the following characteristics of your choice:

outlaw:investigator::Misdirection.text: Beginning at 13th level, you can sometimes cause another creature to suffer an attack meant for you. When you are targeted by an attack while another creature is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to have the attack target that creature instead of you.

outlaw:investigator::Soul of Deceit.text: Starting at 17th level, your thoughts can’t be read by any means, unless you allow it. You can present false thoughts by making a Charisma (Deception) check contested by the mind reader’s Wisdom (Insight) check.

outlaw:rebooted::Engram Whisper.text: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn how to collect fragments of dead personalities, known as engrams. Whenever you finish a short or long rest, you can gain one skill proficiency and one tool proficiency of your choice, as an engram shares its knowledge with you. You lose these proficiencies when you use this feature to choose different proficiencies that you lack.

outlaw:rebooted::Engram Wail.text: At 3rd level, as you nudge someone closer to the grave, you broadcast the pain from their engrams to a nearby foe. Immediately after you deal your Sneak Attack damage to a creature on your turn, you can target a second creature that you can see within 30 feet of the first creature. Roll half the number of Sneak Attack dice for your level (round up), and the second creature takes entropic damage equal to the roll’s total as their implants try to replicate the damage the engram says they should be suffering.

outlaw:rebooted::Engram Possession.text: At 9th level, when a life ends in your presence, you’re able to permanently download a portion of their digital soul into your memory cache. As a reaction when a sapient creature you can see dies within 30 feet of you, you gain an engram token. This is a digital object that you are considered to always have in your possession unless you are the victim of brain hacking or you store it in a digital crypt.

outlaw:rebooted::Engram Self.text: At 13th level, you can partially digitize yourself, becoming like a ghost. As a bonus action, you assume an incorporeal form. While in this form, you have a flying speed of 10 feet, you can hover, and attack rolls have disadvantage against you. You can also move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain, but you take 1d10 kinetic damage if you end your turn inside a creature or an object.

outlaw:rebooted::Death Knell.text: At 17th level, your knowledge of death has become so deep that you gain the following benefits:

outlaw:scout::Skirmisher.text: Starting at 3rd level, you are difficult to pin down during a fight. You can move up to half your speed as a reaction when an enemy ends its turn within 5 feet of you. This movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks.

outlaw:scout::Survivalist.text: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Nature and Survival skills if you don’t already have it, and you gain expertise in those skills as well.

outlaw:scout::Superior Mobility.text: At 9th level, your walking speed increases by 10 feet. If you have a climbing or swimming speed, this increase applies to that speed as well.

outlaw:scout::Bushwhacker.text: Starting at 13th level, you excel at leading ambushes and acting first in a fight.

outlaw:scout::Sudden Strike.text: Starting at 17th level, you can strike with deadly speed. If you take the Attack action on your turn, you can make one additional attack as a bonus action. This attack can benefit from your Sneak Attack even if you have already used it this turn, but you can’t use your Sneak Attack against the same target more than once in a turn.

outlaw:shard::Biokinetic Power.text: Starting at 3rd level, you harbor a wellspring of biokinetic energy within yourself. This energy is represented by your Biokinetic Energy dice, which are each a d6. You have a number of these dice equal to twice your proficiency bonus, and they fuel various biokinetic powers you have, which are detailed below.

outlaw:shard::Energy Blades.text: Also at 3rd level, you can manifest your biokinetic power as shimmering blades of biokinetic energy. Whenever you take the Attack action, you can manifest an energy blade from your free hand and make the attack with that blade.

outlaw:shard::Mind Knife.text: At 9th level, you have the ability to tune your energy blades to a different frequency, allowing them to disrupt a creature’s nervous system without harming their body. When you make an attack with an Energy Blade, you can choose for it to deal software damage rather than kinetic damage. The blade leaves no mark on its target if it deals damage when you use it in this fashion.

outlaw:shard::Powerful Blades.text: Starting at 9th level, your Energy Blades are fully integrated with your biokinetic implants, giving you these powers that use your Biokinetic Energy dice:

outlaw:shard::Someone Else’s Problem.text: At 13th level, you can weave a veil of psychic static to mask yourself. As an action, you can become invisible, along with anything you are wearing or carrying, for 1 hour or until you dismiss this effect (no action required). This invisibility ends immediately after you deal damage to a creature, or you force a creature to make a saving throw.

outlaw:shard::Focused Totality.text: When you reach 17th level, you can sweep your Energy Blade directly through a creature’s central nervous system. When you use your Energy Blades to deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you can force that target to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Dexterity modifier). If the save fails, the target is stunned for 1 minute. The stunned target can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

outlaw:swashbuckler::Fancy Footwork.text: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn how to land a strike and then slip away without reprisal. During your turn, if you make a melee attack against a creature, that creature can’t make opportunity attacks against you for the rest of your turn.

outlaw:swashbuckler::Rakish Audacity.text: Starting at 3rd level, your confidence propels you into battle. You can give yourself a bonus to your initiative rolls equal to your Charisma modifier.

outlaw:swashbuckler::Panache.text: At 9th level, your charm becomes extraordinarily beguiling. As an action, you can make a Charisma (Persuasion) check contested by a creature’s Wisdom (Insight) check. The creature must be able to hear you, and the two of you must share a language.

outlaw:swashbuckler::Elegant Maneuver.text: Starting at 13th level, you can use a bonus action on your turn to gain advantage on the next Dexterity (Acrobatics) or Strength (Athletics) check you make during the same turn.

outlaw:swashbuckler::Master Duelist.text: Beginning at 17th level, your mastery of the blade lets you turn failure into success in combat. If you miss with an attack roll, you can roll it again with advantage. Once you do so, you can’t use this feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

outlaw:thief::Fast Hands.text: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, use your thief’s tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.

outlaw:thief::Traceur.text: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement.

outlaw:thief::Supreme Sneak.text: Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on a Dexterity (Stealth) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

outlaw:thief::Tech Dilettante.text: By 13th level, you have learned enough about the workings of tech that you can improvise the use of tech items even when they are not intended for you. You ignore all class, race, and level requirements on the use of tech items.

outlaw:thief::Impossible Reflexes.text: When you reach 17th level, you have become adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal initiative and your second turn at your initiative minus 10. You can’t use this feature when you are surprised.

pretender::LiNKER Screening.text: Beginning at 1st level, you have been screened for and dosed with LiNKER, a dangerous, one-of-a-kind secret drug compound that artificially induces a high sync rate between flesh and machine, instilling a certain instinct for technology. You have advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks to track software-based creature types and hacked, as well as on Intelligence ability checks to recall information about them.

pretender::Biotech Sequencing.text: At 1st level, you gain the ability to direct, and sometimes overcharge, the nanophage fueling itself upon you to hyperanalyze and disrupt the connection between creatures and their own nanite colonies. You gain two Sequence Breaches of your choice. You learn an additional Sequence Breach of your choice at 3rd level, and can choose a Sequence Breach you know and replace it with a different Sequence Breach. This occurs again at 6th, 11th, 15th, 18th, and 20th level as shown by the Pretender table.

pretender::Lethal Error.text: At 2nd level, you learned how to induce a controlled external surge of your nanophage, at the expense of each sacrificed nanite lancing a crash report of pain through you. You learn a Hardware Error of your choice.

pretender::Fighting Style.text: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a FIghting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

pretender::Pretender's Mask.text: At 3rd level, you commit yourself to the imitation of a dedicated archetype. The mask you choose grants you features at 3rd, 7th, 11th, 15th, and 18th level.

pretender::Ability Score Improvement.text: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

pretender::Extra Attack.text: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

pretender::Retributive Monitor Chip.text: At 6th level, when you damage a creature using your Lethal Error feature, you can choose to condense your nanophage into a tracking chit within them. You always know the direction to the chipped creature, and once per round, when it deals damage to you or a creature you can see within 5 feet of you, the chipped creature takes software damage equal to your Nanophage modifier.

pretender::Seen Some Shit.text: When you reach 9th level, your ever-present paranoia of being caught up in your lies has scarred every suspicious sight into the back of your mind. When making an Intelligence (History) check to recall information about a dark or circumspect past surrounding an object you are touching, or a location you are present in, you have advantage on the roll. The information gleaned often leans towards the sinister or conspiratorial influences of the past, and sometimes conveys information previously unknown to the character on higher rolls at the fixer's discretion, through stress-induced visions and crackpot theory breakthroughs.

pretender::LiNKER ADY-Refinement.text: Upon reaching 10th level, you are called in for a second LiNKER screening, a new, personalized, dosage permanently allowing you to reinforce yourself and further integrate with your nanophage colony. Your speed increases by 10 feet, you gain nightvision out to 60 feet, if you already have nightvision, extend it by an additional 30 feet. Whenever you make a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution saving throw, you can spend and roll a Nanophage Die, reducing your hit points by the result of the roll, to instead make a saving throw with your Nanophage ability score.

pretender::Monitor Chip Upgrade: Lockdow.text: Starting at 13th level, you can maintain wireless access with the chips manifested of your nanophage and enact a direct denial of service. The software damage from your Retributive Monitor Chip increases to twice your Nanophage modifier (minimum of 2).

pretender::Tired and Jaded.text: When you reach 14th level, the shit you've seen has numbed you to attempts of piercing your guise, whether they be to shake or entice you. You have advantage on saving throws against being charmed and frightened.

pretender::So That's As Far As You Can G.text: At 17th level, you refuse to let your nanophage alone choose the limits of your self-deception and push the absolute limit of risk and reward. Once per turn, when you would spend a Nanophage Die, you can instead spend four hit dice. If you would roll the Nanophage Dice, instead roll all four hit dice, losing hit points equal to the total roll.

pretender::Perfect Synchronization.text: At 20th level, the pain of your nanophage has numbed, it's unconscious as breathing. There is no longer any identifiable division between what is you, nanite, and constituent parts. While your hit points are below half your hit point maximum, the damage die for your Lethal Errors becomes d12s. While your hit points are below one fourth your hit point maximum, the damage rolled for your Lethal Errors is maximized.

pretender:genome-freak::Maxims.text: When you don this mask at 3rd level, you begin to develop aphormorphic, psychosomatic compounds that temporarily alter the malleability and stress responses of your self. You gain four Fleshweave Maxims of your choice. You learn an additional Maxim of your choice at 7th level, and can choose a Maxim you know and replace it with a different Maxim. This occurs again at 11th, 15th, and 18th level.

pretender:genome-freak::Fleshweave.text: Also at 3rd level, you can concoct a single maxim you know when you finish a short or long rest. At 7th level, the number of maxims you can concoct when finishing a short or long rest increases by one. This occurs again at 15th and 20th level.

pretender:genome-freak::All Fucked Up.text: At 7th level, the constant reshaping of your body, from cell to surface, has made you resillient to other sources of genetic alteration and nucleotide corrosion. You gain immunity to poison damage and the poisoned condition, though can choose to be affected by any individual instance of poison damage or the poisoned condition.

pretender:genome-freak::Monitor Chip Upg.text: At 11th level, your Retributive Monitor Chip can analyze and enforce a target's source code or genome. Any deceptions or technical effects disguising or making a creature invisible immediately end when you chip them, and they cannot benefit from such deceptions or technical effects while chipped. If a creature is reformated or redefined when you chip it, or attempts to reformat or redefine while chipped, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or revert to its true form or have the attempt fail and be stunned until the end of your next turn.

pretender:genome-freak::Xenomorphic Blee.text: At 15th level, you've inherited the peaks of your own advancements into your base state of being, primed to endure and retaliate against even theoretical hazards. You gain the following benefit:

pretender:genome-freak::Absolute Evosync.text: At 18th level, the mask has become the face, and every mutable flaw of the body, be it blot, dent, or virus, has become yours to command. Your ability to act as a carrier for an effect you are otherwise immune to now applies to poisons in addition to diseases, and you can act as a carrier for up to three effects, choosing which one you lose and a creature saves against when you are hit with a melee attack.

pretender:pact-shill::Sponsored Speciali.text: When you reach 3rd level, you strike a bargain with a commercial sponsor of your choice detailed by the streamer class. Your choice augments some of your mask features. In addition, you learn both 1st and 2nd level techs from your sponsor's expanded tech list. PACT Shills sponsored by VPN Corp gain the expanded techs of the appropriate level from one column of your choice in addition to the phasic column, this distinction applies to your future mask features.

pretender:pact-shill::Gifted Tech.text: Also at 3rd level, your sponsor allocates a product-image defense budget, granting you access to techs and the streamer tech list.

pretender:pact-shill::Crash Report.text: Beginning at 3rd level, your biotechnical imprint acts as a foothold for your sponsor's range of influence. While you have an active Lethal Error, you can use the hyperlinked weapon as a techcasting focus for your streamer techs, and when you cast a trick you deal additional damage equal to your Lethal Error. You deal this additional damage once per casting of a trick.

pretender:pact-shill::Safe-Class Promoti.text: At 7th level, your sponsor has analyzed you as more benefit than cost and granted you confidential access to tech usually reservered for their stars. You learn both the 3rd level techs from your sponsor's expanded tech list and may cast each tech once without expending a tech slot, regaining the ability to do so with this feature on a long rest.

pretender:pact-shill::Battle Souvenir.text: Starting at 7th level, when you use your action to cast a trick, you can immediately make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

pretender:pact-shill::Monitor Chip Upgra.text: At 11th level, your Retributive Monitor Chip can isolate an individual nanite colony's Inherent Protocol address and secretly mark it for isolation and technical destruction. A creature chipped by you has disadvantage on its saving throws against your streamer techs.

pretender:pact-shill::Euclid-Class Promo.text: At 15th level, your sponsor has deemed you an asset of equivalent value to the typical livestream staff team and granted you restricted tech access. You learn both the 4th level techs from your sponsor's expanded tech list and may cast each tech once without expending a tech slot, regaining the ability to do so with this feature on a long rest.

pretender:pact-shill::Keter-Class Promot.text: At 18th level, your sponsor reveals that your work up until now has merely been a test of loyalty and granted your secret access to techs that elude even some of their streamers. You learn both the 5th level techs from your sponsor's expanded tech list and may cast each tech once without expending a tech slot, regaining the ability to do so with this feature on a long rest.

pretender:pact-shill::Absolute Capitasyn.text: At 18th level, the mask has become the face, you can manipulate your persona as finely as your sponsor, having realized the truth that all modern profit is built on a back of suffering and making it look pretty for the camera. Instead of spending a tech slot to cast a tech, you can instead spend and roll a number of hit dice equal to twice the level of slot you would spend for the level you intend to cast the tech. The tech is then cast at that level, and you lose hit points equal to the total rolled. You can cast techs with this feature a number of times equal to your Nanophage modifier (minimum of once), regaining all uses when you finish a long rest.

pretender:risen-servo::Humanoid-Hacked F.text: When you don this mask at 3rd level, you sear a line in the sand of your self to maintain the distinction of what is and isn't hacked. You gain the following benefit:

pretender:risen-servo::Net Escape.text: Upon reaching 7th level, at start of your turn, if you aren't incapacitated, you can choose to technically escape between realms, using your early modwares as a digitization relay.

pretender:risen-servo::Monitor Chip Upgr.text: At 11th level, your Retributive Monitor Chip can act as a pull-up/pull-down signal interface that ensures a known state and strength, setting up targets for the same errors that fuel your weapons. Whenever you damage a chipped creature with your lethal error, your weapon deals an additional Nanophage Potency of the hyperlinked error's damage. In addition, the chipped creature cannot move through other creatures or objects through any means.

pretender:risen-servo::LiNKER Receptor M.text: At 15th level, you've taken to outdated machine and cybernetic mods with illegal modifications that retroactively write your personality data into your LiNKER Screening results, warding it from hacked. You cannot be charmed or frightened by hacked, nor can you be possessed.

pretender:risen-servo::Absolute Datasync.text: At 18th level, the mask has become the face, you have made a mockery of the immortality of software and nested it in flesh and metal, as every hacked has failed to do, your very thoughts strung out between every byte and error. When you are reduced to 0 hit points while you wield a weapon with a hyperlinked lethal error, you can choose to end the hyperlinked lethal error to drop to 1 hit point instead. If you have multiple lethal errors hyperlinked on different weapons, you can choose which one ends.

pretender:sipping-strain::Hacked-Humanoi.text: When you don this mask at 3rd level, you piece together and integrate out-of-date prosthesis to channel bodily augmentations in the image of netsuckers. You gain the following benefit:

pretender:sipping-strain::Nanoransom Seq.text: Also at 3rd level, your Sequence Breaches incorporate a simulation of the injection and biopaywall programs that form the basis of a 'sucker's bite. When you would cannibalize yourself for a Sequence Breach, you can choose for your nanophage to forcibly integrate the nanites they disrupt. Instead of losing hit points equal to your Nanophage Potency, you inflict the result as damage to the target of your Sequence Breach, the damage type being chosen from the Lethal Errors you know. You then regain hit points equal to the damage dealt.

pretender:sipping-strain::Hackjob Flitte.text: At 7th level, you've hobbled together the hardware to traverse the air and maneuver the battlefield with ease. As a bonus action, you can activate your hackjob, possibly going partially digital or growing hardlight wings in reverence of a proper strain, or deploying joint-mounted jets to make your own of it, gaining a flying speed equal to your walking speed. By expending a Nanophage Die, rolling it and reducing your hit points by the total amount, you can activate this flight as a reaction, and immediately move up to half your speed without triggering opportunity attacks. This flight lasts for 1 hour. At the end of the duration, you slowly fall back down to the ground at a safe speed.

pretender:sipping-strain::Monitor Chip U.text: At 11th level, your Retributive Monitor Chip can act as a microtized manufactorum, eating away at your victims for substance. As a bonus action, you can cause a creature chipped by you within 60 feet to lose hit points equal to two rolls of your Nanophage Potency. You then heal for half the result.

pretender:sipping-strain::Biotech Nanovo.text: At 15th level, your mastery of your faux-ransomware expands. Whenever one of your Sequence Breaches ends on a hostile creature, you can choose to draw their nanites into their blood as your nanophage retreats, dealing entropic damage to them equal to your Pretender level.

pretender:sipping-strain::Absolute Hemos.text: At 18th level, the mask has become the face, and your nanomanipulative abilities culminate in total hemotechnical control. When you would regain hit points as a result of your Nanoransom Sequencing, Monitor Chip Upgrade: Autodrain, or Biotech Nanovoracity features, you can choose to forgo healing to instead gain a charge of Hemotech.

pretender:snarling-beast::Pheromonal Mar.text: When you don this mask at 3rd level, you begin to exist in a state of twilight between critter and person, senses honed like that of a natural predator. You gain advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on hearing or smell.

pretender:snarling-beast::Beast Mode Min.text: Upon donning this mask at 3rd level, you have hybridized your nanophage to respond to specific chemical sequences aligned with pseudolegal splicing procedures. As a bonus action, you can directly alter your phenotype to express these splices, assuming your Beast Mode for up to 1 hour. You can still speak, use equipment, and wear armor in this form. You can revert to your true form earlier as a bonus action, and do so automatically when falling unconscious, dropping to 0 hit points, or when dead.

pretender:snarling-beast::Instinctual Ru.text: At 7th level, the twilight state of your senses primes your body for the hunt, the grand everchase. Your speed increases by 10 feet. You also add 10 feet to your long jump distance and 3 feet to your high jump distance.

pretender:snarling-beast::Monitor Chip U.text: At 11th level, your Retributive Monitor Chip can signal your animal senses, ringing out marrow deep like a dinner bell, directing a deep and unending hunger to draw your savagery. While in Beast Mode, your attacks have advantage against a chipped target. Additionally, as the intensity of your hunger acts as an undercurrent to your force of presence, you gain proficiency in Charisma saving throws.

pretender:snarling-beast::Beast Mode Maj.text: Starting at 15th level, your nanophage-splice hybrid has mutated alignment with your genetic sequence and base code, keeping the beast within close at hand. You can activate your Beast Mode a third time between short or long rests.

pretender:snarling-beast::Absolute Thero.text: At 18th level, the mask has become the face, you have mastered your hybridization and married instinct with elevated human thought, the twilight of your urges becoming a constant invitation, be it night or day. When you have expended all uses of your Beast Mode activation, you can instead enter Beast Mode by spending and rolling two Nanophage Dice, losing hit points equal to the total.

renegade::Hype.text: In battle, you hype yourself up to incredible emotional heights. On your turn, you can get hype as a bonus action.

renegade::Unarmored Defense.text: While you are not wearing any armor, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier. You can use a shield and still gain this benefit.

renegade::Reckless Attack.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

renegade::Danger Sense.text: At 2nd level, you gain an uncanny sense of when things nearby aren’t as they should be, giving you an edge when you dodge away from danger.

renegade::Passionate Path.text: At 3rd level, the nature of your passion and the means by which you tap into it begin to shape your abilities. Your hype might come from primal fury, heedless joy, crazed lust, or some other emotion. Choose one of the Passionate Paths presented at the end of this class. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th levels.

renegade::Ability Score Improvement.text: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

renegade::Extra Attack.text: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

renegade::Fast Movement.text: Starting at 5th level, your speed increases by 10 feet while you aren’t wearing heavy armor.

renegade::Tweaked Instinct.text: By 7th level, your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls.

renegade::Brutal Critical.text: Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack.

renegade::Relentless Hype.text: Starting at 11th level, your hype can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while you are hype and don’t die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead.

renegade::Persistent Hype.text: Beginning at 15th level, your passion is so fierce that your hype only ends early if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.

renegade::Indomitable Might.text: Beginning at 18th level, if your total for a Strength check is less than your Strength score, you can use that score in place of the total.

renegade::Perpetual Hype.text: At 20th level, you embody the all-consuming power of hype. Your Strength and Constitution ability scores increase by 4, and your Strength and Constitution maximum ability scores also increase by 4.

renegade:bouncer::Frenzy.text: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can go into a frenzy when you get hype. If you do so, for the duration of your hype you can make a single melee weapon attack as a bonus action on each of your turns after this one. When your hype ends, you suffer one level of exhaustion (PHB Appendix A).

renegade:bouncer::Heedless Hype.text: Beginning at 6th level, you can’t be charmed or frightened while hype. If you are charmed or frightened when you get hype, the effect is suspended for the duration of your hype.

renegade:bouncer::Intimidating Presence.text: Beginning at 10th level, you can use your action to frighten someone with your menacing presence. When you do, choose one creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. If the creature can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier) or be frightened of you until the end of your next turn. On subsequent turns, you can use your action to extend the duration of this effect on the frightened creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends if the creature ends its turn out of line of sight or more than 60 feet away from you.

renegade:bouncer::Retaliation.text: Starting at 14th level, when you take damage from a creature that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature.

renegade:dervish::Leather Daddy.text: When you choose this path at 3rd level, you gain the ability to use spiked armor as a weapon.

renegade:dervish::Feeling No Pain.text: Beginning at 6th level, when you use Reckless Attack while hype, you also gain temporary hit points equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1). These temporary hit points are lost if any of them remain when your hype ends.

renegade:dervish::Tweaker’s Charge.text: Beginning at 10th level, you can take the Dash action as a bonus action while you are hype.

renegade:dervish::Spiked Reacharound.text: Starting at 14th level, when a creature within 5 feet of you hits with a melee attack, the attacker takes your Strength modifier in piercing damage. To use this ability, you must be hype, not incapacitated, and wearing spiked armor.

renegade:dirty-fighter::Hidden Weapons.text: Starting at 3rd level, when you get hype, you can unveil your hidden weapon modifications. Until the hype ends, you manifest a natural weapon. This weapon counts as a civilian melee weapon for you, and you add your Strength modifier to attack and damage rolls with the weapon as normal.

renegade:dirty-fighter::Hidden Mods.text: Your process of surreptitiously upgrading yourself continues at 6th level. Your natural weapons gained from your Hidden Weapons feature count as tech weapons for purposes of overcoming resistance and immunity.

renegade:dirty-fighter::Infectious Hype.text: Starting at 10th level, when you hit a creature with your natural weapons while you are hype, you can fill the target with an overpowering rage, lust, frustration, or similar wild passion. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus) or suffer one of the following effects (your choice):

renegade:dirty-fighter::Gang Bang.text: Beginning at 14th level, you master the art of the gang bang, gaining strength from others even as they gain strength from you. When you get hype, you can choose a number of willing creatures you can see within 30 feet of you equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1). You gain 5 temporary hit points for each creature that accepts your gift of hype. Until your hype ends, the chosen creatures can roll a bonus d6 of damage on one successful attack each turn.

renegade:juggernaut::Unstoppable Force.text: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, you can channel your unstoppable fury into your weapon strikes. While you are hype, the first creature you hit on each of your turns with a weapon attack takes extra damage equal to 1d6 + half your renegade level. When you gain this feature, choose whether the extra damage is entropic, kinetic, or neon.

renegade:juggernaut::Lust for Life.text: At 3rd level, your hype is so strong that others have a much easier time calling you back from death. If a tech, such as [raise dead], has the sole effect of restoring you to life (but not reanimating you as one of the hacked), the tech has no monetary cost to use on you.

renegade:juggernaut::Immovable Object.text: Starting at 6th level, the passion that fuels your hype can protect you from harm. If you fail a saving throw while hype, you can reroll it; you must use the new roll.

renegade:juggernaut::Life of the Party.text: At 10th level, your infectious hype inspires others to let loose as well. As a bonus action, you unleash a battle cry that can be heard up to 60 feet away. Up to ten other creatures of your choice within that area who can hear you gain advantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the start of your next turn.

renegade:juggernaut::Beyond Death.text: Beginning at 14th level, the power that fuels your hype allows you to shrug off fatal blows. While you are hype, having 0 hit points doesn’t knock you unconscious. You must still make death saving throws, and you suffer the normal effects of taking damage while at 0 hit points. However, if you would die due to failing death saving throws, you don’t die until your hype ends, and you die then only if you still have 0 hit points.

renegade:maelstrom-psycho::Tech Awarenes.text: Starting at 3rd level, as an action, you can open your awareness to the presence of tech besides your own. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of any active tech or tech item within 60 feet of you that isn’t behind total cover. When you sense a tech power, you learn which type of tech it is.

renegade:maelstrom-psycho::Psycho Tech.text: The weird tech you’ve wired into your brain sometimes spills out around you. When you get hype, roll on the Psycho Tech table below to determine the tech effect produced. If the effect requires a saving throw, the DC is 8 + your Constitution modifier + your proficiency bonus.

renegade:maelstrom-psycho::Bolstering Te.text: You can harness your freaky implants to bolster yourself or a companion beginning at 6th level. As an action, you can touch one creature (which can be yourself) and confer one of the following benefits of your choice to the target:

renegade:maelstrom-psycho::Maelstrom Bac.text: Beginning at 10th level, your psycho implants have a tendency to destructively reboot when you are imperiled. After you suffer damage or fail a saving throw while hype, you can use your reaction to roll on the Psycho Tech table and immediately produce the effect rolled. This effect replaces your current Psycho Tech effect.

renegade:maelstrom-psycho::Controlled Br.text: From 14th level on, whenever you roll on the Psycho Tech table, you can roll the die twice and choose which of the two effects to unleash. If you roll the same number on both dice, you can ignore the number and choose any effect on the table.

renegade:splicer::Beast Kin.text: Animals just get you, man—and you get them. At 3rd level when you adopt this path, you gain the ability to use the pack leader and Doolittle's dialog techs, but only as scripts.

renegade:splicer::Beast Splicing.text: At 3rd level when you adopt this path, you choose a category of beasts from the list below and gain the feature associated with it. You gain minor physical attributes that are reminiscent of a beast from that category. For example, if you choose Powerful Beast, you might be unusually hairy like a bear or gain the antlers of a moose, while choosing Stalking Beast might grant you vertical slits in your eyes like a tiger or a wolf-like muzzle.

renegade:splicer::Bestial Aspect.text: At 6th level, you gain a benefit based on a new beast you splice into your body profile. You can choose the same beast as you selected at 3rd level or a different one. Your physical features morph yet further to reflect your new selection.

renegade:splicer::Beast Link.text: At 10th level, you can use the Wide Area Diagnostic tech, but only as a script. When you do so, your mind connects wirelessly to every animal in the area, granting you a gestalt impression of the information you seek.

renegade:splicer::Bestial Attunement.text: At 14th level, you gain a benefit based on a new beast you splice into your body profile. You can choose the same beast as you selected at any previous level or a different one. Your physical features become more bestial still.

renegade:stand-user::Stand Projection.text: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, a spectral warrior (“Stand”) appears when you get hype. While you’re hype, the first creature you hit with an attack on your turn becomes the Stand’s target. Until the start of your next turn, that target has disadvantage on any attack roll that isn’t against you, and when the target hits a creature other than you with an attack, that creature has resistance to the damage dealt by the attack. The effect on the target ends if your hype ends.

renegade:stand-user::Stand Shield.text: Beginning at 6th level, your Stand can provide protection to you or those you defend. While you are hype, if you or another creature you can see within 30 feet suffers damage, you can use your reaction to reduce that damage by 2d6.
