renegade:stand-user::Stand Surveillance.text: At 10th level, you gain the ability to consult with your Stand directly, utilizing its extensive passive and active sensor suite on your behalf. You may use the magic 8-ball or stealth drone techs without using a tech slot or requiring a focus. Rather than creating a sensor, this use of stealth drone invisibly transports your Stand to the chosen location, allowing you to see through its eyes, and returns it to your location when the tech’s duration ends. Wisdom is your focus ability for these techs.

renegade:stand-user::Stand Vengeance.text: At 14th level, your Stand grows powerful enough to retaliate against your foes. When you use your Stand Shield to reduce the damage of an attack, the attacker takes an amount of kinetic damage equal to the damage that your Stand Shield prevents.

renegade:tempest::Tempest Aura.text: Starting at 3rd level, you emanate a tech-based aura when you get hype. This aura extends 10 feet from you in every direction, but not through total cover.

renegade:tempest::Tempest Hardened.text: At 6th level, your implants grant you benefits even when you are not actively hyped up. The benefits are based on your current environment choice for your Tempest Aura.

renegade:tempest::Tempest Shielded.text: At 10th level, you learn to use your environment-manipulating implants to protect others. Each creature of your choice in the area of your Storm Aura has the damage resistance you gain from the Tempest Hardened feature.

renegade:tempest::Category Six.text: At 14th level, your environment-generating implants reach their maximum potency, allowing you to lash out at your foes. The benefits are based on your current environment choice for your Tempest Aura.

renegade:unstoppable::Outta The Way.text: Starting when you choose this path at 3rd level, your hype mingles with an unspeakable cocktail of aftereffects lingering inside you to push you and your enemies further. When you hit a creature with a melee attack while you're hyped up, you can push that creature up to 5 feet away from you in a direction of your choice. A creature that is Huge or larger makes a Strength saving throw with a DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier. On a success, the creature is not pushed.

renegade:unstoppable::Shift Your Weight.text: At 3rd level, you've figured out that standing still gets you killed. You never truly stop, bouncing around even when you're still. While you are hyped, you can't be knocked prone or moved along the ground against your will.

renegade:unstoppable::Tear It Down.text: Starting at 6th level, your melee weapon attacks deal an extra 1d8 damage to machines, and deal double damage to objects and structures.

renegade:unstoppable::Don't Let 'Em Catc.text: Also at 6th level, you can lose yourself to your personal rhythm, like the ingrained beat of the last party you blacked out at. At the start of your turn, no action required, you can get jiggy with it until the start of your next turn. While defensively dancing, you can't be grappled, attack rolls against you have disadvantage, and your weapon attacks are made with disadvantage.

renegade:unstoppable::Mosh Pit.text: Starting at 10th level, you've mastered shoving posers into the trampling of true fans. As a reaction when you push a creature at least 5 feet, you can then leap into an unoccupied space next to the creature. If you do so, the creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw with a DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier or be knocked prone. This leap costs no movement and does not provoke opportunity attacks.

renegade:unstoppable::Can't Feel Nothin'.text: At 14th level, even running on fumes gives you that good buzz, numbing you to the fetters of life. While you're hyped, your speed cannot be reduced, and you are immune to the frightened, paralyzed, prone, rattled and stunned conditions.

ronin::Fighting Style.text: You adopt a particular style of fighting as your specialty. Choose one of the following options. You can't take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.

ronin::Second Wind.text: You have a limited well of stamina that you can draw on to protect yourself from harm. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your ronin level.

ronin::Action Surge.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can push yourself beyond your normal limits for a moment. On your turn, you can take one additional action.

ronin::Martial Archetype.text: At 3rd level, you choose an archetype that you strive to emulate in your combat styles and techniques. The archetype you choose grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th, 10th, 15th, and 18th level.

ronin::Ability Score Improvement.text: When you reach 4th level, and again at 6th, 8th, 12th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

ronin::Martial Versatility.text: Whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can do one of the following, as you shift the focus of your martial practice:

ronin::Extra Attack.text: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

ronin::Indomitable.text: Beginning at 9th level, you can reroll a saving throw that you fail. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

ronin:biker::Bonus Proficiency.text: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Animal Handling, History, Insight, Performance, or Persuasion. You also gain proficiency with either motorcycles or muscle cars. If you were already proficient with the chosen vehicle, you instead gain expertise.

ronin:biker::Creature of the Wheel.text: Starting at 3rd level, your mastery as a driver becomes apparent. You have advantage on saving throws made to avoid wrecking your vehicle. If you wreck your vehicle, you suffer only half damage and are not Stunned by the wreck.

ronin:biker::Unwavering Mark.text: Starting at 3rd level, you can menace your foes, foiling their attacks and punishing them for harming others. When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can mark the creature until the end of your next turn. This effect ends early if you are incapacitated or you die, or if someone else marks the creature.

ronin:biker::Swerving Maneuver.text: At 7th level, you learn to fend off strikes directed at you, your vehicle, or other creatures nearby. If you, your vehicle, or a creature you can see within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can roll 1d8 as a reaction if you’re wielding a melee weapon or a shield. Roll the die, and add the number rolled to the target’s AC against that attack. If the attack still hits, the target has resistance against the attack’s damage.

ronin:biker::Hold the Line.text: At 10th level, you become a master of locking down your enemies. Creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they move 5 feet or more while within your reach, and if you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the target’s speed is reduced to 0 until the end of the current turn.

ronin:biker::Hell on Wheels.text: Starting at 15th level, you can run down your foes, whether you’re driving or not. If you move at least 10 feet in a straight line right before attacking a creature and you hit it with the attack, that target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or be knocked prone. You can use this feature only once on each of your turns.

ronin:biker::Vigilant Defender.text: Starting at 18th level, you respond to danger with extraordinary vigilance. In combat, you get a special reaction that you can take once on every creature’s turn, except your turn. You can use this special reaction only to make an opportunity attack, and you can’t use it on the same turn that you take your normal reaction.

ronin:codebreaker::Bonus Proficiencies.text: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with the programmer’s kit.

ronin:codebreaker::Code Fragments.text: Starting at 3rd level, you can use fragments of ancient code to enhance your gear. You learn two codes of your choice, from among the codes described below, and each time you gain a level in this class, you can replace one code you know with a different one from this feature. When you reach certain levels in this class, you learn additional codes, as shown in the Codes Known table.

ronin:codebreaker::Hulk Out.text: At 3rd level, you have learned how to briefly alter your own genetic code to become a hulking monster. As a bonus action, you gain the following benefits, which last for 1 minute:

ronin:codebreaker::Short Circuit.text: At 7th level, you learn to invoke your code fragments to protect your allies. When another creature you can see within 60 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, you can use your reaction to force the attacker to reroll the d20 and use the new roll.

ronin:codebreaker::Great Stature.text: By 10th level, your mastery of your own genetic code permanently alters you. When you gain this feature, roll 3d4. You grow a number of inches in height equal to the roll. You permanently gain the Powerful Build quality, allowing you to count as one size larger than your actual size for purposes of carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

ronin:codebreaker::Code Master.text: At 15th level, you can invoke each code you know from your Code Fragments feature twice, rather than once, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

ronin:codebreaker::Truly Massive.text: At 18th level, you learn how to amplify your genetic transformation. As a result, the extra damage you deal with the Hulk Out feature increases to 1d10. Moreover, when you use that feature, your size can increase to Huge, and while you are that size, your reach increases by 5 feet.

ronin:crazed-killer::Dreadful Presence.text: Beginning when you choose this archetype at 3rd level, as a bonus action on your turn, you can activate your Dreadful Presence for 1 minute. You can end your Dreadful Presence early using another bonus action, and it also ends early if you fall unconscious. You determine how this presence visually manifests by rolling on the following table or deciding for yourself.

ronin:crazed-killer::Killer Skills.text: At 3rd level, to represent your murderous methods, you have a number of killer dice equal to your proficiency bonus, which are d6s. You regain all of your expended killer dice when you finish a short or long rest. Your killer dice improve as you gain fighter levels, becoming d8s at 10th level and d10s at 18th level.

ronin:crazed-killer::Soulless Efficiency.text: At 7th level, you have become eerily detached from emotion. While your Dreadful Presence is active, you are immune to being charmed or frightened. If you are being affected by one of these conditions when you activate your Dreadful Presence, the effect is suspended for the duration.

ronin:crazed-killer::Inescapable Hunter.text: At 10th level, while a creature is frightened by your Dreadful Presence, for the next hour, you always know its location so long as it is on the same plane as you and is not invisible, and nonmagical difficult terrain costs you no extra movement while you are moving directly towards it.

ronin:crazed-killer::Ceaseless Torment.text: At 15th level, when a creature succeeds on its save against your Dreadful Presence, it only remains immune to that feature until you hit it with a weapon attack. Additionally, when you roll initiative and have no killer dice remaining, you regain 1 killer die.

ronin:crazed-killer::Jump-Scaring Stalke.text: At 18th level, you are able to seemingly move with the shadows themselves and appear as if from nowhere to scare the life out your quarry. While your Dreadful Presence is active, you can use a bonus action to become invisible until the start of your next turn or until you take an action. While you are invisible, your walking speed increases by 10 feet. If you end your invisibility by taking the Attack action and hit a creature with an attack as part of that action, the creature has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against your Dreadful Presence.

ronin:exile::No Rest For The Wicked.text: Beginning when you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you become immune to physical exhaustion, or fatigue, as the result of your own actions, such as long periods of travel or extended periods of physical strain and activity. Fatigue caused by specific features, abilities, or effects still applies.

ronin:exile::Can't Slow Down.text: Also at 3rd level, you've learned that the only true path of survival is one of constant motion, and so refuse to rest or let your injuries slow your assault. You gain two additional uses of your second wind feature. When you use a bonus action to regain hit points using your second wind feature, you can also choose to expend a number of hit dice up to your proficiency Bonus to gain a number of temporary hit points equal to the number rolled + your Constitution modifier, and you can make one weapon attack as part of the same bonus action. Starting at 7th level, this attack is made at advantage.

ronin:exile::Can't Hold Back.text: Starting at 7th level, you gain resistance to entropic and poison damage, and you have advantage on saving throws against disease and exhaustion. Your grim disposition puts off even the approach of death, you add half of your Intimidation modifier to your death saving throws. Once per long rest, if applying this bonus increases the total to a 20 or higher, you gain the benefits of rolling a 20 on the d20.

ronin:exile::Cracked Reactions.text: At 10th level, you conserve your energy where you can, a corpse like stillness giving way to frenzied retaliation when least expected, allowing you to recoup on another man's time. You gain two additional uses of your second wind feature, for a total of four additional uses. When you are hit with an attack, you can use your reaction to tank the blow, immediately using your second wind, making an attack with the same reaction as per can't slow down. If the triggering attack does not deplete the temporary hit points gained from can't slow down, you can make an additional attack as part of the same reaction, and move up to half your movement, without triggering opportunity attacks, before doing so.

ronin:exile::Until We Close Our Eyes.text: Starting at 15th level, you are immune to disease, exhaustion from non-technical sources, and you have advantage on saving throws against the poisoned, unconscious, and incapacitated conditions. Whenever you roll initiative or return to 1 hit point as a result of rolling a 20 on a death save, you can expend and roll one hit die, gaining an amount of hit points equal to the roll + your Constitution modifier.

ronin:exile::Die On Your Feet.text: At 18th level, your hardships have allowed you to thoroughly straddle the border between life and death and call it your bitch. You gain two additional uses of your second wind feature, for a total of six additional uses. You do not lose consciousness or become incapacitated while at 0 hit points, and taking damage while you are at 0 hit points does not impose any failed death saves. You can not take actions, reactions, or move while in this state, except for taking a bonus action to automatically fail one death save, which then allows you to take the rest of your turn as normal.

ronin:hardlight-soldier::Hardlight Refle.text: At 3rd level, you can use a bonus action to manifest a hardlight reflection of yourself in an unoccupied space you can see within 15 feet of you. This echo is a tech-based, translucent image of you that lasts until it is destroyed, until you dismiss it as a bonus action, until you manifest another echo, or until you’re incapacitated.

ronin:hardlight-soldier::Unleash Incarna.text: At 3rd level, you can heighten your reflection's fury. Whenever you take the Attack action, you can make one additional melee attack from the reflection's position.

ronin:hardlight-soldier::Hardlight Avata.text: Starting at 7th level, you can temporarily transfer your consciousness to your reflection. As an action, you can see through your reflection's eyes and hear through its ears. During this time, you are deafened and blinded. You can sustain this effect for up to 10 minutes, and you can end it at any time (requires no action). While your reflection is being used in this way, it can be up to 1,000 feet away from you without being destroyed.

ronin:hardlight-soldier::Martyr in the M.text: Starting at 10th level, you can make your reflection throw itself in front of an attack directed at another creature that you can see. Before the attack roll is made, you can use your reaction to teleport the reflection to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the targeted creature. The attack roll that triggered the reaction is instead made against your reflection.

ronin:hardlight-soldier::Reclamation of.text: By 15th level, you've learned to absorb the fleeting potential energy in your reflection. When a reflection of yours is destroyed by taking damage, you can gain a number of temporary hit points equal to 2d6 + your Constitution modifier, provided you don't already have temporary hit points.

ronin:hardlight-soldier::Legion of One.text: At 18th level, you can use a bonus action to create two reflections with your Hardlight Reflection feature, and these reflections can co-exist. If you try to create a third reflection, the previous two reflections are destroyed. Anything you can do from one reflection's position can be done from the reflections' instead.

ronin:old-warlord::Improved Critical.text: Beginning when you choose this archetype at 3rd level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

ronin:old-warlord::Remarkable Athlete.text: Starting at 7th level, you can add half your proficiency bonus (rounded up) to any Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution check you make that doesn’t already use your proficiency bonus.

ronin:old-warlord::Additional Fighting S.text: At 10th level, you can choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature.

ronin:old-warlord::Superior Critical.text: Starting at 15th level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20.

ronin:old-warlord::Survivor.text: At 18th level, you attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle. At the start of each of your turns, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left. You don’t gain this benefit if you have 0 hit points.

ronin:special-operative::Biokinetic Powe.text: At 3rd level, you are implanted with a series of hyper-dense batteries that grant you a special energy resource. This energy is represented by your Biokinetic Energy dice, which are each a d6. You have a number of these dice equal to twice your proficiency bonus, and they fuel various powers you have, which are detailed below.

ronin:special-operative::Biokinetic Adep.text: By 7th level, you have mastered new ways to use your biokinetic abilities, detailed below.

ronin:special-operative::Guarded Mind.text: Starting at 10th level, the Biokinetic Energy flowing through you has bolstered your mind. You have resistance to software damage. Moreover, if you start your turn charmed or frightened, you can expend a Biokinetic Energy die and end every effect on yourself subjecting you to those conditions.

ronin:special-operative::Force Field.text: At 15th level, you can shield yourself and others with biokinetic force. As a bonus action, you can choose creatures, which can include you, that you can see within 30 feet of you, up to a number of creatures equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one creature). Each of the chosen creatures is protected by half cover for 1 minute or until you’re incapacitated.

ronin:special-operative::Biokinetic Mast.text: By 18th level, your ability to move creatures and objects with your mind is matched by few. You can cast the nanokinesis tech, requiring no components, and your techcasting ability for the tech is Intelligence. On each of your turns while you concentrate on the tech, including the turn when you cast it, you can make one attack with a weapon as a bonus action.

ronin:speed-demon::Action Before Thought.text: Starting at 3rd level, your enhancements allow your body to move faster than thought. When you would be hit be an attack roll, you can use your reaction to immediately move 5 feet, without triggering opportunity attacks, as long as you do not end this movement further from the target than when you began it. If the triggering attack was a ranged attack, you can choose to stay stationary. When you complete this movement, roll 1d6. On a roll of 4 or higher, the triggering attack instead misses you. On a 3 or lower, you gain resistance to the damage of the triggering attack.

ronin:speed-demon::Hyper-Speed Augmentat.text: Additionally at 3rd level, the enhancements that allow your body to move faster manifest minimum activation benefits. Your movement speed is increased by 5 feet. Your movement speed further increases by 10 feet at 11th level, and by 15 feet at 18th level.

ronin:speed-demon::Chemically-Induced Pr.text: Starting at 7th level, you have advantage on initiative rolls. In addition, you are immune to being surprised while conscious.

ronin:speed-demon::Improved Augmentation.text: Also starting at 7th level, your chosen Hyper-Speed Augmentation gains new abilities.

ronin:speed-demon::Warp Dancer.text: Starting at 10th level, when you cause an attack to miss you with the Action Before Thought feature, you can use Action Before Thought against the next attack made against you, without spending your reaction or a use of the feature. When causing an attack to miss in this way, you can still make a Head-Hunter's Riposte. This effect remains in effect, triggered by itself, until an attack misses you as a result of anything other than the Action Before Thought feature or the Action Before Thought feature fails to cause an attack to miss.

ronin:speed-demon::Stimulant Overdrive.text: Starting at 15th level, you can use your stimulant injectors to push your body to it's limits. You may cast the overdrive tech as a free action, targeting yourself. It can still be dissipated as normal, but you do not suffer the lethargy effects from the effect ending.

ronin:speed-demon::Superior Augmentation.text: Also starting at 15th level, your chosen Hyper-Speed Augmentation gains new abilities.

ronin:speed-demon::Stimulant Rampage.text: Starting at 18th level, as soon as you strike an enemy down, you can use that moment to unleash hell upon your enemies.

ronin:street-samurai::Bonus Proficiency.text: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: History, Insight, Performance, or Persuasion. Alternatively, you gain proficiency with a vehicle or tool kit of your choice.

ronin:street-samurai::Spirit of the Samu.text: Starting at 3rd level, your intensity in battle can shield you and help you strike true. As a bonus action on your turn, you can give yourself advantage on all weapon attack rolls until the end of the current turn. When you do so, you also gain 5 temporary hit points. The number of hit points increases when you reach certain levels in this class, increasing to 10 at 10th level and 15 at 15th level.

ronin:street-samurai::Intense Self-Contr.text: Starting at 7th level, your discipline and attention to detail allow you to excel in social situations. Whenever you make a Charisma (Persuasion) check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 0).

ronin:street-samurai::Raging Spirit.text: Starting at 10th level, when you roll initiative and have no uses of Spirit of the Samurai remaining, you regain one use.

ronin:street-samurai::Rapid Strike.text: Starting at 15th level, you learn to trade accuracy for swift strikes. If you take the Attack action on your turn and have advantage on an attack roll against one of the targets, you can forego the advantage for that roll to make an additional weapon attack against that target, as part of the same action. You can do so no more than once per turn.

ronin:street-samurai::Last Stand.text: Starting at 18th level, your spirit can even delay the hand of death itself. If you take damage that reduces you to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to delay falling unconscious, and you can immediately take an extra turn. While you have 0 hit points during that extra turn, taking damage causes death saving throw failures as normal, and three death saving throw failures can still kill you. When the extra turn ends, you fall unconscious if you still have 0 hit points.

ronin:tactical-sniper::Basic Tech.text: At 3rd level, you learn some basic tech abilities, as well as gaining knowledge of either wilderness survival or the theory behind your advanced capabilities. You choose to gain proficiency in either the Technology or Survival skill, and you choose to learn either the nanotech twiddling or neetcraft trick.

ronin:tactical-sniper::Trick Shot.text: At 3rd level, you learn to unleash special tech effects with some of your shots. When you gain this feature, you learn two Trick Shot options of your choice.

ronin:tactical-sniper::Tech Shot.text: At 7th level, you gain the ability to infuse bullets with enhanced power. Whenever you fire a mundane bullet from a firearm without the loading property, you can make it tech for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to mundane attacks and damage. The power fades from the bullet immediately after it hits or misses its target.

ronin:tactical-sniper::Curve the Bullet.text: At 7th level, you learn how to direct a bullet arrow toward a new target. When you make an attack roll with a tech bullet and miss, you can use a bonus action to reroll the attack roll against a different target within 60 feet of the original target.

ronin:tactical-sniper::Ever-Ready Shot.text: Starting at 15th level, your empowered gunplay is available whenever battle starts. If you roll initiative and have no uses of Trick Shot remaining, you regain one use of it.

ronin:tactical-sniper::Trick Shot Option.text: The Trick Shot feature lets you choose options for it at certain levels. The options are presented here in alphabetical order. They are all tech effects, as though the shot were enhanced by a trick-level tech.

ronin:tactician::Combat Superiority.text: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn maneuvers that are fueled by special dice called superiority dice.

ronin:tactician::Student of Battle.text: At 3rd level, you gain proficiency with one type of tool kit of your choice, or with the Culture or History skill.

ronin:tactician::Know Your Enemy.text: Starting at 7th level, if you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own. The DM tells you if the creature is your equal, superior, or inferior in regard to two of the following characteristics of your choice:

ronin:tactician::Improved Combat Superio.text: At 10th level, your superiority dice turn into d10s. At 18th level, they turn into d12s.

ronin:tactician::Relentless.text: Starting at 15th level, when you roll initiative and have no superiority dice remaining, you regain 1 superiority die.

ronin:technoblade::Techcasting.text: When you reach 3rd level, you augment your martial prowess with the ability to cast spells.

ronin:technoblade::Weapon Bond.text: At 3rd level, you learn how to upgrade one weapon you own with tech. You perform the modification over the course of 1 hour, which can be done during a short rest. The weapon must be within your reach throughout the process, at the conclusion of which you touch the weapon and forge a biometric bond with it.

ronin:technoblade::Battle Synergy.text: Beginning at 7th level, when you use your action to cast a trick, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

ronin:technoblade::Techno Strike.text: At 10th level, you learn how to make your weapon strikes undercut a creature’s resistance to your techs. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, that creature has disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes against a tech you cast before the end of your next turn.

ronin:technoblade::Quantum Charge.text: At 15th level, you gain the ability to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see when you use your Action Surge. You can teleport before or after the additional action.

ronin:technoblade::Improved Techno Strik.text: Starting at 18th level, when you use your action to cast a tech, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

ronin:vanguard::Stirring Shout.text: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you learn how to inspire your allies to fight on past their injuries.

ronin:vanguard::Natural Leader.text: Leaders are expected to have some level of diplomatic ability, no matter how rough around the edges they might be normally.

ronin:vanguard::Inspiring Surge.text: Starting at 10th level, when you use your Action Surge feature, you can choose one creature within 60 feet of you that is allied with you. That creature can make one melee or ranged weapon attack with its reaction, provided that it can see or hear you.

ronin:vanguard::Bastion.text: Beginning at 15th level, you can extend the benefit of your Indomitable feature to an ally. When you decide to use Indomitable to reroll an Intelligence, a Wisdom, or a Charisma saving throw and you aren’t incapacitated, you can choose one ally within 60 feet of you that also failed its saving throw against the same effect. If that creature can see or hear you, it can reroll its saving throw and must use the new roll.

ronin:warlord::Improved Critical.text: Beginning when you choose this archetype at 3rd level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20.

ronin:warlord::Improved Fighting Style.text: Additionally at 3rd level, your selected Ronin fighting style is further refined. You gain the following the bonus based on your Fighting Style:

ronin:warlord::Remarkable Athlete.text: Starting at 7th level, you gain proficiency in Athletics. If you already have proficiency in Athletics, you can add twice your Proficiency bonus to your Athletics checks.

ronin:warlord::Superior Critical.text: Starting at 7th level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 18-20.

ronin:warlord::Additional Fighting Style.text: At 10th level, you can choose a second option from the Fighting Style class feature.

ronin:warlord::Determination.text: Starting at 15th level, you can attempt to use physical prowess to break through technical effects that are otherwise physically impassable. As an action, you can make a Strength (Athletics) check against the tech save DC of the techcaster to attempt to force your way through technical barriers or effects. On a success, you can move up through the effect, spending four feet of movement for each foot moved through the effect.

ronin:warlord::Ultimate Critical.text: Starting at 15th level, your weapon attacks score a critical hit on a roll of 17-20.

ronin:warlord::Survivor.text: At 18th level, you attain the pinnacle of resilience in battle. At the start of each of your turns, you regain hit points equal to 5 + your Constitution modifier if you have no more than half of your hit points left. You don’t gain this benefit if you have 0 hit points.

ronin:warlord::Fighting Mastery.text: Additionally at 18th level, you gain the benefits of Improved Fighting Style for the fighting style you gain from your 10th level feature.

shutin::Shut-In Slang.text: You know Shut-In Slang, the secret language of Shut-Ins. You can speak the language and use it to leave hidden messages. You and others who know this language automatically spot such a message. Others spot the message's presence with a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check but can't decipher it without tech.

shutin::Techcasting.text: You can cast tech that shape your SLUDGE to your will.

shutin::Goo Shape.text: SLUDGE, as a nutrition rich substance, is best fitted to replicating the shape and musculature of beasts, their Shut-In Goo-borne forms being denoted as Combat Units. Starting at 2nd level, you can use your action to mold your SLUDGE around you into such a Combat Unit. You can use this feature twice. You regain expended uses when you finish a short or long rest.

shutin::Shut-In Complex.text: At 2nd level, your Complex begins to define your actions as a Shut-In. Your choice grants you features at 2nd level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

shutin::Goo Companion.text: At 2nd level, you gain the ability to create a SLUDGE construct that assumes an animal form: as an action, you can expend a use of your Goo Shape feature to cast the Find Familiar tech, without material components.

shutin::Ability Score Improvement.text: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

shutin::Trick Versatility.text: Whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace one Trick you learned from this class's techcasting feature with another Trick from the Shut-In tech list.

shutin::Timeless Body.text: Starting at 18th level, the time spent controlling your avatar causes you to age more slowly. For every 10 years that pass, your body ages only 1 year.

shutin::Goo Casting.text: Beginning at 18th level, you can cast many of your Shut-In techs in any shape you assume using Goo Shape. You can perform the somatic and verbal components of a Shut-In tech while in a Goo shape, but you aren't able to provide material components.

shutin::Uber Shut-In.text: At 20th level, you can use your Goo Shape an unlimited number of times.

shutin:astrologist::Chart the Heavens.text: At 2nd level, you've created a star chart as part of your endless collection of alternative medicine. It is a Tiny object and can serve as a techcasting focus for your Shut-In techs. You determine and describe its form.

shutin:astrologist::Cosmic Form.text: At 2nd level, you gain the ability to harness the alleged power of horoscopes to alter your form. As a bonus action, you can expend a use of your Goo Shape feature to take on a glowing, cosmic form, rather than transforming into a beast.

shutin:astrologist::Augury of the Stars.text: When you reach 6th level, you learn to use your star map to divine the will of the cosmos. Whenever you finish a long rest, you can consult your Star Map for omens. When you do so, roll a die. Until you finish your next long rest, you gain access to a special reaction based on whether you rolled an even or an odd number on the die:

shutin:astrologist::The Shifting Expanse.text: At 10th level, the constellations of your Cosmic Form improve. The 1d8 of the Gunslinger and the Thermos becomes 2d8, and while the Kaiju is active, you have a flying speed of 20 feet and can hover.

shutin:astrologist::Galactic Being.text: At 14th level, while in your Cosmic Form, you become partially incorporeal, giving you resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.

shutin:biome::Bonus Trick.text: When you choose this complex at 2nd level, you learn one additional Shut-In trick of your choice.

shutin:biome::Practicing Self-Care.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can regain some of your energy by sitting in meditation and communing with the imagined nature of the etherealnet… During a short rest, you choose expended tech slots to recover. The tech slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your Shut-In level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher. You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

shutin:biome::Sense Techs.text: Your connection to the Sense-Tanks infuses you with the ability to cast certain techs. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to Sense techs connected to your favorite digital biome. Choose that land: arctic, coast, desert, forest, grassland, mountain, swamp, or Undercity. Consult the associated list of techs with your land.

shutin:biome::Easy Strider.text: Starting at 6th level, moving through non-digital difficult terrain costs you no extra movement. You can also pass through non-digital plants without being slowed by them and without taking damage from them if they have thorns, spines, or a similar hazard.

shutin:biome::Imagined Naturalist.text: When you reach 10th level, you can't be charmed or frightened by surges or spam, and you are immune to poison and disease.

shutin:biome::Gruff Appearance.text: When you reach 14th level, creatures of the real world sense your bizarre inclinations towards nature and become hesitant to attack you. When a beast or plant creature attacks you, that creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your Shut-In tech save DC. On a failed save, the creature must choose a different target, or the attack automatically misses. On a successful save, the creature is immune to this effect for 24 hours.

shutin:geek::Rife With Nanotechnology.text: At 2nd level, your NEET powers extra compartments of healing nanobots. You are a font of energy that offers respite from injuries. You have a pool of energy represented by a number of d6s equal to your Shut-In level.

shutin:geek::Home Is Where The Drone Is.text: At 6th level, home can be wherever you are. During a short or long rest, you can surround yourself in a cloaking sphere to help guard your respite. At the start of the rest, you touch a point in space, and an invisible, 30-foot-radius sphere of tech appears, centered on that point. Total cover blocks the sphere.

shutin:geek::Net Runner.text: Starting at 10th level, you digitize yourself to Blink across the battlefield. As a bonus action on your turn, you can teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Alternatively, you can use your action to teleport one willing creature you touch up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

shutin:geek::Walker in Dreams.text: At 14th level, your experience with your NEET grants you the ability to travel mentally or physically through the Corpo-Net or Dark Web with ease.

shutin:hacker::Sense Techs.text: Your symbiotic link to your nanobot caches grants you access to certain techs. At 2nd level, you learn the entropic virus trick.

shutin:hacker::Halo of Nanobots.text: Starting at 2nd level, you are surrounded by invisible, entropic nanobots that are harmless until you unleash them on a creature nearby. When a creature you can see moves into a space within 10 feet of you or starts its turn there, you can use your reaction to deal 1d4 entropic damage to that creature unless it succeeds on a Constitution saving throw against your tech save DC. The entropic damage increases to 1d6 at 6th level, 1d8 at 10th level, and 1d10 at 14th level.

shutin:hacker::Nanobot Symbiote.text: Also at 2nd level, you gain the ability to channel repairing tech into your nanobots. As an action, you can expend a use of your Goo Shape feature to awaken those nanobots, rather than transforming into a new form, and you gain 4 temporary hit points for each level you have in this class. While this feature is active, you gain the following benefits:

shutin:hacker::Reconstitute Corpse.text: At 6th level, your nanobots gain the ability to infest a robotic corpse and animate it. If a critter or a humanoid that is Small or Medium dies within 10 feet of you, you can use your reaction to animate it, causing it to stand up immediately with 1 hit point. The creature uses the Tech Husk stat block in the enemies list. It remains animated for 1 hour, after which time it collapses and dies.

shutin:hacker::Spreading Nanobots.text: At 10th level, you gain the ability to seed an area with deadly nanobots. As a bonus action while your Nanobot Symbiote feature is active, you can hurl nanobots up to 30 feet away, where they swirl in a 10-foot cube for 1 minute. The nanobots disappear early if you use this feature again, if you dismiss them as a bonus action, or if your Symbiotic Entity feature is no longer active.

shutin:hacker::Souped Up Avatar.text: At 14th level, the nanobots in your NEET alter you: you can't be blinded, deafened, frightened, or poisoned, and any critical hit against you counts as a normal hit instead, unless you're incapacitated.

shutin:herder::Speech of the Woods.text: At 2nd level, you gain the ability to converse with beasts of all shapes and sizes… as well as a few spam.

shutin:herder::Animal Projection.text: Starting at 2nd level, you gain the ability to project holographic animals and use them to influence the world around you.

shutin:herder::Mighty Hardlighter.text: At 6th level, beasts and spam that you project are more resilient than normal. Any beast or spam summoned or created by a tech that you cast gains two benefits:

shutin:herder::Stalwart Hologram.text: Beginning at 10th level, your hologram projector safeguards the beasts and spam that you call forth with your tech. When a beast or spam that you summoned or created with a tech ends its turn in your hologram projector aura, that creature regains a number of hit points equal to half your Shut-In level.

shutin:herder::Separate Power Source.text: Starting at 14th level, the digital holograms you create protect you when you are the most defenseless. If you are reduced to 0 hit points or are incapacitated against your will, you can immediately gain the benefits of digistruct critters as if it were cast with a 9th-level tech slot. It creates four beasts of your choice that are challenge rating 2 or lower. The conjured beasts appear within 20 feet of you. If they receive no commands from you, they protect you from harm and attack your foes. The tech lasts for 1 hour, requiring no concentration, or until you dismiss it (no action required).

shutin:pyro::Sense Techs.text: When you join this Sense at 2nd level, you have fabricated a fire-formed Chibi. Your link with this Chibi grants you access to some techs when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Sense of fire-formed techs table.

shutin:pyro::Summon Fire-Formed Chibi.text: At 2nd level, you can create a fire-formed chibi. As an action, you can expend one use of your Goo Shape feature to summon your fire-formed chibi, rather than assuming a beast form.

shutin:pyro::Adorable Bond.text: At 6th level, the bond with your fire-formed Chibi enhances your destructive and restorative techs. Whenever you cast a tech that deals fire damage or restores hit points while your fire-formed Chibi is summoned, roll a d8, and you gain a bonus equal to the number rolled to one damage or healing roll of the tech.

shutin:pyro::Field on Fire.text: At 10th level, you gain the ability to turn corpses into flames that can heal or incinerate. When a Small or larger creature dies within 30 feet of you or your fire-formed Chibi, a countdown notification appears on your hud in the dead creature's space and flickers there for 1 minute. When a creature you can see enters that space, you can use your reaction to either heal the creature or deal fire damage to it. The healing or damage equals 2d10 + your Wisdom modifier.

shutin:pyro::Burning Bright.text: At 14th level, the bond with your fire-formed Chibi can save you from death. If the Chibi is within 120 feet of you when you are reduced to 0 hit points and thereby fall unconscious, you can cause the Chibi to drop to 0 hit points. You then regain half your hit points and immediately rise to your feet.

shutin:surger::Combat Goo Shape.text: When you choose this Sense at 2nd level, you gain the ability to use Goo Shape on your turn as a bonus action, rather than as an action.

shutin:surger::Perfect Forms.text: Your desire for the perfect Combat Unit grants you the ability to transform into more dangerous animals. Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Goo Shape to transform into a beast with a challenge rating as high as 1. You ignore the max CR column of the Goo Shapes table but must abide by the other limitations there.

shutin:surger::Goo-Enhanced Strike.text: Starting at 6th level, your attacks in beast form count as technical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nontechnical attacks and damage.

shutin:surger::Surge Goo Shape.text: At 10th level, you can expend two uses of Goo Shape at the same time to transform into an air Surge, an earth Surge, a fire Surge, or a water Surge.

shutin:surger::Thousand Forms.text: By 14th level, you have learned to use tech to alter your physical form in more subtle ways. You can cast the temporary surgery tech at will.

sourcecoder::Techcasting.text: An event in your past left an indelible mark on you, infusing you with ancient code. This source code, whatever its origin, fuels and informs your techs.

sourcecoder::Code Origin.text: Choose a code origin, which describes the code you tapped into during the event that turned you into a source coder and its manifestations since. Your choice grants you features when you choose it at 1st level and again at 6th, 14th, and 18th level.

sourcecoder::Inner Power.text: At 2nd level, you tap into a deep wellspring of power within yourself. This inner power is represented by source points, which allow you to create a variety of magical effects.

sourcecoder::Metatech.text: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to twist your techs to suit your needs. You gain two of the following Metatech options of your choice. You gain another one at 10th and 17th level.

sourcecoder::Ability Score Improvement.text: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

sourcecoder::Code Versatility.text: When you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can do one of the following, representing the code within you flowing in new ways:

sourcecoder::Code Guidance.text: When you reach 5th level, you can tap into your inner power to try and snatch success from failure. When you make an ability check that fails, you can spend 1 source point to reroll the d20, and you must use the new roll, potentially turning the failure into a success.

sourcecoder:arc-caster::Weather Forecast.text: You have an intuitive knowledge of the current and upcoming weather. You can always sense the air temperature, humidity, and current weather conditions within one mile of you, even if you are underground or indoors. You can also determine the weather a number of days into the future equal to your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier (minimum of one day). This forecast is perfectly accurate, short of being altered or manipulated by techs or similar special powers.

sourcecoder:arc-caster::Tempest Tossed.text: Starting at 1st level, you can use a bonus action on your turn to cause whirling gusts of air to briefly surround you, immediately before or after you cast a tech of 1st level or higher. Doing so allows you to fly up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.

sourcecoder:arc-caster::Tempest Hardened.text: At 6th level, you gain resistance to lightning and thunder damage. In addition, whenever you start casting a tech of 1st level or higher that deals lightning or thunder damage, electrostatic power erupts from you. This eruption causes creatures of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of you to take lightning or thunder damage (choose each time this ability activates) equal to half your source coder level.

sourcecoder:arc-caster::Storm Guide.text: At 6th level, you gain the ability to subtly control the weather around you.

sourcecoder:arc-caster::Storm’s Fury.text: Starting at 14th level, when you are hit by a melee attack, you can use your reaction to deal lightning damage to the attacker. The damage equals your source coder level. The attacker must also make a Strength saving throw against your source coder tech save DC. On a failed save, the attacker is pushed in a straight line up to 20 feet away from you.

sourcecoder:arc-caster::Wind Waker.text: At 18th level, you gain immunity to lightning and thunder damage.

sourcecoder:astro-mahou::Celestial Embod.text: At 1st level you learn additional techs when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Astronomy Techs table. Each tech counts as a source coder tech for you, but it doesn’t count against the number of source coder techs you know. These techs can’t be replaced when you gain a level in this class.

sourcecoder:astro-mahou::Shine Down Spar.text: Starting at 1st level, you can call down the radiant light of the nighttime skybox on command. You learn the neon shower tech, which doesn't count against the number of source coder tricks you know. When you cast the tech, you can target one creature as normal or target two creatures within range that are within 5 feet of each other.

sourcecoder:astro-mahou::Placement of Go.text: Beginning at 6th level, the current position of your Celestial Embodiment can affect your Metatech feature. Each Celestial Embodiment position is associated with certain sectors of tech, as shown here:

sourcecoder:astro-mahou::Spatial Realign.text: At 6th level, you gain greater control over the positions of your space-based technology. As a bonus action, you can spend 1 source point to change your current Celestial Embodiment phase to a different one.

sourcecoder:astro-mahou::The Horoscope's.text: Beginning at 14th level, the power of a astral position saturates your being. While you are in a Celestial Embodiment phase, you also gain the following benefit associated with that position:

sourcecoder:astro-mahou::Cosmic Power, T.text: At 18th level, as a bonus action, you can tap into a special power of your current Celestial Embodiment position. Alternatively, as part of the bonus action you take to change your astral position using the Spatial Realignment feature, you can immediately use the power of the astral position you are entering:

sourcecoder:beta-tester::Beta Bug.text: Starting when you choose this origin at 1st level, your techcasting can unleash unpredictable tech effects. Immediately after you cast a source coder tech of 1st level or higher, the DM can have you roll a d20. If you roll a 1, roll on the Beta Bug table to create a random tech effect.

sourcecoder:beta-tester::Probability Man.text: Starting at 1st level, you can manipulate the forces of chance and chaos to gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. Once you do so, you must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again.

sourcecoder:beta-tester::Bend Luck.text: Starting at 6th level, you have the ability to alter quantum probability for others as well as yourself. When another creature you can see makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction and spend 2 source points to roll 1d4 and apply the number rolled as a bonus or penalty (your choice) to the creature’s roll. You can do so after the creature rolls but before any effects of the roll occur.

sourcecoder:beta-tester::Controlled Chao.text: At 14th level, you gain a modicum of control over the bugs inherent in your tech. Whenever you roll on the Beta Bug table, you can roll twice and use either number.

sourcecoder:beta-tester::Tech Bombardmen.text: Beginning at 18th level, the harmful energy of your techs intensifies. When you roll damage for a tech and roll the highest number possible on any of the dice, choose one of those dice, roll it again and add that roll to the damage. You can use the feature only once per turn.

sourcecoder:circuitist::Circuitboard Tec.text: You learn additional techs when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Circuitboard Techs table. Each tech counts as a source coder tech for you, but it doesn't count against the number of source coder techs you know.

sourcecoder:circuitist::Circuit Unbroken.text: Starting at 1st level, you can release the stored energy within your circuits to absorb or deflect threatening attacks. Whenever you take damage, you can expend any number of [ACTIVE] circuits as a reaction. Roll a number of d6s equal to the number of circuits you expended, and reduce the damage by the total.

sourcecoder:circuitist::The Flesh is Wea.text: At 6th level, you can redirect your circuits to flow through your muscles rather than your nanites and blood. When you make a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution ability check or saving throw, you can expend an [ACTIVE] circuit as a reaction to gain advantage on the roll. Once you use this feature to grant yourself advantage on a saving throw, you can't use this feature that way again until you complete a long rest.

sourcecoder:circuitist::The Code is Will.text: Also at 6th level, you can reveal hidden nanotech runes and technical barriers that surround you. As an action, you expend 1 [ACTIVE] circuit to reveal hidden or invisible technical traps, marks, nanotech runes, setups, firewalls, or sensors within 60 feet of you. They glow with dim light in a 5-foot radius for 1 minute.

sourcecoder:circuitist::Short Circuit.text: Upon reaching 14th level, you can redirect and funnel energy to overpower even the most insulated of barriers. When you cast a tech, you can expend 2 [ACTIVE] circuits to cause the tech to deal kinetic damage instead of its usual damage types.

sourcecoder:circuitist::01100101 0111100.text: Starting at 18th level, you can use a bonus action and expend an [ACTIVE] circuit to sublimate your physical vessel across local nanites, transmission signals, and your own circuits. While partially discorporated in such a way, you gain the following benefits:

sourcecoder:cyber-valkyrie::Divine Right.text: Your link to pantheon code allows you to learn techs normally associated with ordinators. When your Techcasting feature lets you learn a source coder trick or a source coder tech of 1st level or higher, you can choose the new tech from the ordinator tech list or the source coder tech list. You must otherwise obey all the restrictions for selecting the tech, and it becomes a source coder tech for you.

sourcecoder:cyber-valkyrie::AI Assisted.text: Starting at 1st level, your actions are guided by the incredible computing power of a pantheon. If you fail a saving throw or miss with an attack roll, you can roll 2d4 and add it to the total, possibly changing the outcome.

sourcecoder:cyber-valkyrie::Empowered He.text: Starting at 6th level, your mastery of pantheon code can empower your healing techs. Whenever you or an ally within 5 feet of you rolls dice to determine the number of hit points a tech restores, you can spend 1 source point to reroll any number of those dice once, provided you aren’t incapacitated. You can use this feature only once per turn.

sourcecoder:cyber-valkyrie::Hardlight Wi.text: Starting at 14th level, you can use a bonus action to manifest a pair of hardlight wings from your back. While the wings are present, you have a flying speed of 30 feet. The wings last until you’re incapacitated, you die, or you dismiss them as a bonus action.

sourcecoder:cyber-valkyrie::Unearthly Re.text: At 18th level, you gain the ability to overcome grievous injuries. As a bonus action when you have fewer than half of your hit points remaining, you can regain a number of hit points equal to half your hit point maximum.

sourcecoder:neuromancer::Neural Techs.text: When you choose this origin at 1st level, you gain the neurojack trick in addition to your chosen tricks.

sourcecoder:neuromancer::Neural Link.text: Starting at 1st level, you can form a mental connection between your mind and the mind of another. As a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You and the chosen creature can speak mentally with each other while the two of you are within a number of miles of each other equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1 mile). To understand each other, you each must speak mentally in a language the other knows.

sourcecoder:neuromancer::Neuromancy.text: Beginning at 6th level, when you cast any tech of 1st level or higher from your Neural Techs feature, you can cast it by expending a tech slot as normal or by spending a number of source points equal to the tech’s level. If you cast the tech using source points, it has no verbal or somatic requirements, and it requires no material requirements, unless they are consumed by the tech.

sourcecoder:neuromancer::Mental Firewall.text: At 6th level, you gain resistance to software damage, and you have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened.

sourcecoder:neuromancer::Nightmarish For.text: Beginning at 14th level, you can unleash a form drawn from the worst nightmares of others. As a bonus action, you can spend 1 or more source points to transform your body for 10 minutes.

sourcecoder:neuromancer::Haptic Implosio.text: At 18th level, you can mentally force yourself into a digitized state, allowing rapid—if dangerous—movement through space.

sourcecoder:surge-splicer::Surge Splice.text: At 1st level, you choose one state of matter to which you have been surge spliced. The damage type associated with each surge is used by features you gain later.

sourcecoder:surge-splicer::Surge Resilie.text: As surgetech alters your body, it causes physical traits of your matter state affinity to emerge. At 1st level, your hit point maximum increases by 1 and increases by 1 again whenever you gain a level in this class.

sourcecoder:surge-splicer::Surge Power.text: Starting at 6th level, when you cast a tech that deals damage of the type associated with your surge affinity, add your Charisma modifier to that damage. At the same time, you can spend 1 source point to gain resistance to that damage type for 1 hour.

sourcecoder:surge-splicer::Surge Movemen.text: At 14th level, you gain the ability to gain a special form of movement related to your surge affinity. You can adopt this movement form as a bonus action on your turn. It lasts until you dismiss it as a bonus action on your turn.

sourcecoder:surge-splicer::Inhuman Prese.text: Beginning at 18th level, you can channel the alien presence of an embodied surge, causing those around you to become awestruck or frightened. As an action, you can spend 5 source points to draw on this power and exude an aura of awe or fear (your choice) to a distance of 60 feet. For 1 minute or until you lose your concentration (as if you were casting a concentration tech), each hostile creature that starts its turn in this aura must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed (if you chose awe) or frightened (if you chose fear) until the aura ends. A creature that succeeds on this saving throw is immune to your aura for 24 hours.

sourcecoder:tech-support::Clockwork Tech.text: You learn additional techs when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Clockwork Techs table. Each tech counts as a source coder tech for you, but it doesn’t count against the number of source coder techs you know. These techs can’t be replaced when you gain a level in this class.

sourcecoder:tech-support::Restore Balanc.text: Starting at 1st level, your understanding of a tech’s median operating state allows you to equalize chaotic moments. When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you is about to roll a d20 with advantage or disadvantage, you can use your reaction to prevent the roll from being affected by advantage and disadvantage.

sourcecoder:tech-support::Fractal Shield.text: Starting at 6th level, you can tap into your understanding of the source code to imbue a creature with a field that disrupts incoming damage. As an action, you can expend 1 to 5 source points to create a fractal field around yourself or another creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The field lasts until you finish a long rest or until you use this feature again.

sourcecoder:tech-support::Stabilizing Al.text: Starting at 14th level, you gain the ability to align your consciousness to the endless calculations of the source code. As a bonus action, you can enter this state for 1 minute. For the duration, attack rolls against you can’t benefit from advantage, and whenever you make an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can treat a roll of 9 or lower on the d20 as a 10.

sourcecoder:tech-support::Fractal Burst.text: At 18th level, you generate a sudden burst of crystalline order that stabilizes reality around you. As an action, you generate a burst of energy in a 30-foot cube originating from you. The burst causes the following effects:

sourcecoder:void-walker::Eyes of the Dar.text: From 1st level, you have darkvision with a range of 120 feet. You do not need to breathe, except to speak, but you are still vulnerable to inhaled toxins and poisons.

sourcecoder:void-walker::Tardigrade Toug.text: Starting at 1st level, your ability to survive even in the void of space makes you difficult to defeat. When damage reduces you to 0 hit points, you can make a Charisma saving throw (DC 5 + the damage taken). On a success, you instead drop to 1 hit point. You can’t use this feature if you are reduced to 0 hit points by neon damage or by a critical hit.

sourcecoder:void-walker::Spatial Anomaly.text: At 6th level, you gain the ability to call forth a blot of living dark matter to harass your foes. As a bonus action, you can spend 3 source points to summon a dark matter hound to target one creature you can see within 120 feet of you. The hound uses the dire wolf’s statistics, with the following changes:

sourcecoder:void-walker::Shadow Blink.text: At 14th level, you gain the ability to step from one shadow into another. When you are in dim light or darkness, as a bonus action, you can teleport up to 120 feet to an unoccupied space you can see that is also in dim light or darkness.

sourcecoder:void-walker::Quantum Form.text: Starting at 18th level, you can spend 6 source points as a bonus action to transform yourself into a half-real quantum state. In this form, you have resistance to all damage except kinetic and neon damage, and you can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. You take 5 kinetic damage if you end your turn inside an object.

streamer::Sponsored Stream.text: At 1st level, you have struck a bargain with a commercial sponsor of your choice. Your choice grants you features at 1st level and again at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

streamer::Gifted Tech.text: The gifts and merch bestowed on you by your patron have given you access to techs.

streamer::Partnership Programs.text: Your sponsors often offer Partnership Programs with various smaller companies, granting you unusual ways of altering and modifying your techs, or granting you strange and unique tech abilities.

streamer::Vibe Boon.text: At 3rd level, your streaming persona becomes more set, leading your sponsor to promote you in specific ways. You gain one of the following features of your choice.

streamer::Ability Score Improvement.text: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

streamer::Programming Versatility.text: Whenever you reach a level in this class that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can do one of the following, representing a change of focus in your occult studies:

streamer::Promotional Tech.text: At 11th level, your sponsor bestows upon you a proprietary tech called a promotional. Choose one 6th-level tech from the streamer tech list as this promotional.

streamer::Top Streamer.text: At 20th level, you are one of the top streamers in the business—still bought and owned, but a valued commodity and a proven brand. You can spend 1 minute messaging your sponsor for aid to regain all your expended tech slots from your Gifted Tech feature. Once you regain tech slots with this feature, you must finish a long rest before you can do so again.

streamer:charity-foundation::Expanded Te.text: The Charity Foundation lets you choose from an expanded list of techs when you learn a streamer tech. The following techs are added to the streamer tech list for you.

streamer:charity-foundation::Bonus Cantr.text: At 1st level, you learn the light transfer and neon shower tricks. They count as streamer tricks for you, but they don’t count against your number of tricks known.

streamer:charity-foundation::Sponsored H.text: At 1st level, you gain the ability to generate injury-seeking nanobots to heal wounds. You have a pool of d6s that you spend to fuel this healing. The number of dice in the pool equals 1 + your streamer level.

streamer:charity-foundation::Living Spot.text: Starting at 6th level, your sponsorship package allows you to serve as a conduit for neon energy. You have resistance to neon damage, and when you cast a tech that deals neon or fire damage, you add your Charisma modifier to one neon or fire damage roll of that tech against one of its targets.

streamer:charity-foundation::Bloom of He.text: Starting at 10th level, you gain temporary hit points whenever you finish a short or long rest. These temporary hit points equal your streamer level + your Charisma modifier. Additionally, choose up to five creatures you can see at the end of the rest. Those creatures each gain temporary hit points equal to half your streamer level + your Charisma modifier.

streamer:charity-foundation::Clean, Pret.text: Starting at 14th level, your sponsorship package allows you to resist death. When you have to make a death saving throw at the start of your turn, you can instead spring back to your feet with a burst of neon energy. You regain hit points equal to half your hit point maximum, and then you stand up if you so choose. Each creature of your choice that is within 30 feet of you takes neon damage equal to 2d8 + your Charisma modifier, and is blinded until the end of the current turn.

streamer:esports::Expanded Tech List.text: The E-Sports Team lets you choose from an expanded list of techs when you learn a streamer tech. The following techs are added to the streamer tech list for you.

streamer:esports::Sportsman’s Mark.text: Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to place a virtual “tag” on someone, known as a mark. As a bonus action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target is marked for 1 minute. The mark ends early if the target dies, you die, or you are incapacitated. Until the mark ends, you gain the following benefits:

streamer:esports::E-Warrior.text: At 1st level, you acquire the training necessary to effectively arm yourself for battle. You gain proficiency with medium armor, shields, and military weapons.

streamer:esports::Humiliation.text: Starting at 6th level, you can humiliate a person you slay, temporarily creating a digital copy of them that serves you. When you slay a humanoid, you can cause a hardlight simulacrum to rise from its corpse as a digital specter. When the specter appears, it gains temporary hit points equal to half your streamer level. Roll initiative for the specter, which has its own turns. It obeys your verbal commands, and it gains a special bonus to its attack rolls equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +0).

streamer:esports::Mark Defense.text: At 10th level, your mark grows more powerful. If the target marked by your Sportsman’s Mark hits you with an attack roll, you can use your reaction to roll a d6. On a 4 or higher, the attack instead misses you, regardless of its roll.

streamer:esports::Masterful Mark.text: Starting at 14th level, you can move your Sportsman’s Mark from a slain creature to another creature. When the creature marked by your Sportsman’s Mark dies, you can apply the mark to a different creature you can see within 30 feet of you, provided you aren’t incapacitated. When you apply the mark in this way, you don’t regain hit points from the death of the previously marked creature.

streamer:gacha-game::Expanded Tech List.text: The Gacha Game lets you choose from an expanded list of techs when you learn a streamer tech. The following techs are added to the streamer tech list for you.

streamer:gacha-game::Digital Leech.text: Starting at 1st level, when you reduce a hostile creature to 0 hit points, you gain temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your streamer level (minimum of 1).

streamer:gacha-game::Gambler’s Luck.text: Starting at 6th level, you can rely on your knowledge of the odds to tilt them in your favor. When you make an ability check or a saving throw, you can use this feature to add a d10 to your roll. You can do so after seeing the initial roll but before any of the roll’s effects occur.

streamer:gacha-game::Thick Skin.text: Starting at 10th level, you can choose one damage type when you finish a short or long rest. You gain resistance to that damage type until you choose a different one with this feature. Damage from tech weapons ignores this resistance.

streamer:gacha-game::Loot Box from Hell.text: Starting at 14th level, when you hit a creature with an attack, you can use this feature to instantly digitize the target and hurl them into a time-accelerated digital realm where they are forced to play mind-numbing games of chance until they accumulate the correct loot items necessary to escape. It only takes a short time in the real world, but it seems like years to the poor soul trapped there.

streamer:goth-topic::Expanded Tech List.text: At 1st level, Goth Topic lets you choose from an expanded list of techs when you learn a streamer tech. The following techs are added to the streamer tech list for you.

streamer:goth-topic::Form of the Goth.text: At 1st level, you can give yourself a temporary glow-up to fully manifest your brand identity. As a bonus action, you transform for 1 minute. You gain the following benefits while transformed:

streamer:goth-topic::Hunger Strike.text: At 6th level, your extensive body modifications have a profound effect on you. You no longer need to eat, drink, or breathe.

streamer:goth-topic::Half-Husk.text: At 10th level, your gothic modifications now saturate your body. You have resistance to entropic damage. If you are transformed using your Form of the Goth, you instead become immune to entropic damage.

streamer:goth-topic::Digital Ghost.text: At 14th level, your consciousness can become untethered from your physical form as a fully-digital engram. As an action, you can project your consciousness from your body. The body you leave behind is unconscious and in a state of suspended animation, apparently dead to all but the closest medical examination.

streamer:hentaihub::Expanded Tech List.text: HentaiHub lets you choose from an expanded list of techs when you learn a streamer tech. The following techs are added to the streamer tech list for you.

streamer:hentaihub::Naughty Tentacle.text: At 1st level, you can generate a hardlight tentacle that strikes at your foes. As a bonus action, you create a 10-foot-long tentacle at a point you can see within 60 feet of you. The tentacle lasts for 1 minute or until you use this feature to create another tentacle.

streamer:hentaihub::Water Sports.text: Also at 1st level, you gain a swimming speed of 40 feet, and you can breathe underwater.

streamer:hentaihub::Casual Nudist.text: At 6th level, you are more at home in your bare skin than in clothing. You gain resistance to cold damage.

streamer:hentaihub::Frisky Tentacle.text: At 6th level, your Naughty Tentacle can defend you and others, interposing itself between them and harm. When you or a creature you can see takes damage while within 10 feet of the tentacle, you can use your reaction to choose one of those creatures and reduce the damage to that creature by 1d8. When you reach 10th level in this class, the damage reduced by the tentacle increases to 2d8.

streamer:hentaihub::Grasping Tentacle.text: Starting at 10th level, you learn the tech ferrofluid tentacles. It counts as a streamer tech for you, but it doesn’t count against the number of techs you know. You can also cast it once without using a tech slot, and you regain the ability to do so when you finish a long rest.

streamer:hentaihub::Livestream.text: When you reach 14th level, you can briefly digitize yourself and piggyback local signals to reach a destination. As an action, you can teleport yourself and up to five other willing creatures that you can see within 30 feet of you. Amid a whirl of tentacles and pixels, you all vanish and then reappear up to 1 mile away, each of you appearing in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of the others. You can only arrive in a location with an active web connection that you have seen before, or one that is currently viewing you live.

streamer:marketing-firm::Expanded Tech L.text: The Marketing Firm lets you choose from an expanded list of techs when you learn a streamer tech. The following techs are added to the streamer tech list for you.

streamer:marketing-firm::Rapid Responses.text: Starting at 1st level, you gain the quick text trick. This trick can be cast as a bonus action and without any components. It counts as a streamer trick, and does not count against your total tricks known.

streamer:marketing-firm::Looking Over My.text: Also at 1st level, your benefactor is always watching. When you fail a Perception, Insight, or Investigation check as well as a Dexterity Saving Throw, you can add your Charisma to the result. This can change the result into a success. Once you turn two failures into successes, you cannot use this feature again until you take a short or long rest.

streamer:marketing-firm::Slippery Advert.text: At 6th level you can make it hard to be focused upon. Using a bonus action, your form is distorted for 1 minute or until your concentration is broken (as if you are concentrating on a tech) as you slip in and out of a frenzied digital advertising spree. Any creature that targets you with a tech or attack must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against your Streamer Save DC. On a failure, they must target a different creature, or the tech or attack is lost. Creatures immune to Software Damage are immune to this feature.

streamer:marketing-firm::Counterargument.text: At 10th level, when you take software damage, make a Wisdom or Intelligence Saving throw, or are sent a telepathic message, you can use your reaction to deal software damage equal to your streamer levels. This can break a creature's concentration on a tech.

streamer:marketing-firm::Aggressive Mark.text: At 14th level, you give into the whims of your benefactor. As an action, you begin spouting off advertisement jargon in rapid fashion. You create an aura of 20 feet around you that can be dismissed with a bonus action. While using this feature, you cannot speak, and can only use tricks or techs from the Marketing Firm expanded tech list.

streamer:survivalist::Expanded Tech List.text: The Survivalist lets you choose from an expanded list of techs when you learn a streamer tech. The following techs are added to the streamer tech list for you.

streamer:survivalist::Not Dead Yet.text: Starting at 1st level, you learn the stabilize trick, which counts as a streamer trick for you. You also have advantage on saving throws against any disease.

streamer:survivalist::Defy Death.text: Starting at 6th level, you can give yourself vitality when you cheat death or when you help someone else cheat it. You can regain hit points equal to 1d8 + your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 hit point) when you succeed on a death saving throw or when you stabilize a creature with stabilize.

streamer:survivalist::Survivor Mods.text: Beginning at 10th level, you can hold your breath indefinitely, and you don’t require food, water, or sleep, although you still require rest to reduce exhaustion and still benefit from finishing short and long rests.

streamer:survivalist::Indestructible Lif.text: When you reach 14th level, your modifications make you very hard to kill indeed. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d8 + your streamer level. Additionally, if you put a severed body part of yours back in place when you use this feature, the part reattaches.

streamer:telecom-provider::Expanded Tech.text: The Telecom Provider lets you choose from an expanded list of techs when you learn a streamer tech. The following techs are added to the streamer tech list for you.

streamer:telecom-provider::Telecom Backd.text: Starting at 1st level, your backdoor into the telecommunications network gives you the ability to touch the minds of other creatures. You can mentally speak to any creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You don’t need to share a language with the creature for it to understand your mental utterances, but the creature must be able to understand at least one language.

streamer:telecom-provider::Combat Teleme.text: At 6th level, you learn to turn an enemy’s failed strike into data you can use to your benefit. When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on that roll. If the attack misses you, your next attack roll against the creature has advantage if you make it before the end of your next turn.

streamer:telecom-provider::Mental Firewa.text: Starting at 10th level, your thoughts can’t be read by any means unless you allow it. You also have resistance to software damage, and whenever a creature deals software damage to you, that creature takes the same amount of damage that you do.

streamer:telecom-provider::Brain Hack.text: At 14th level, you gain the ability to infect a humanoid’s mind with a long-lasting memetic virus. You can use your action to touch an incapacitated humanoid. That creature is then charmed by you until a antivirus tech is cast on it, the charmed condition is removed from it, or you use this feature again.

streamer:vpn-corp::Bound Surge.text: You are always considered to be bound to the phased state of matter. At the end of each long rest, choose one of the other four surges—aqueous, gaseous, plasmic, or solid. You gain the expanded techs and other benefits associated with that surge until the next time you take a long rest.

streamer:vpn-corp::Expanded Tech List.text: At 1st level, the VPN Corp lets you choose from an expanded list of techs when you learn a streamer tech.

streamer:vpn-corp::Virtual Vessel.text: Also at 1st level, your sponsor gifts you a special peripheral that grants you a measure of privacy. The vessel is a Tiny object, and you can use it as a tech focus for your streamer techs. You decide what the object looks like.

streamer:vpn-corp::Surge Resistant.text: At 6th level, your sponsor’s gifts make you resistant to harm from surges. You now have resistance to a damage type determined by your bound surge: bludgeoning (solid), thunder (gaseous), fire (plasmic), or cold (aqueous).
