streamer:vpn-corp::Digital Sanctuary.text: At 10th level, when you enter your Virtual Vessel via the Virtual Respite feature, you can now choose up to five willing creatures that you can see within 30 feet of you, and the chosen creatures are drawn into the vessel with you as digital entities.

streamer:vpn-corp::Direct Entreaty.text: At 14th level, you entreat your sponsor to grant you a minor favor. As an action, you can speak your desire to your Virtual Vessel, requesting the effect of one tech that is 6th level or lower and has a casting time of 1 action. The tech can be from any class’s tech list, and you don’t need to meet the requirements in that tech, including costly components: the tech simply takes effect as part of this action.

streamer:wellness-brand::Expanded Tech L.text: The Wellness Brand lets you choose from an expanded list of techs when you learn a streamer tech. The following techs are added to the streamer tech list for you.

streamer:wellness-brand::Salesperson’s P.text: Starting at 1st level, your sponsor teaches you memetic methods to beguile your audience, or to make them terrified of missing out. As an action, you can cause each creature in a 10-foot cube originating from you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your streamer tech save DC. The creatures that fail their saving throws are all charmed or frightened by you (your choice) until the end of your next turn.

streamer:wellness-brand::Quick Escape.text: Starting at 6th level, you can vanish in a puff of mist in response to harm. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to turn invisible and teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. You remain invisible until the start of your next turn or until you attack or cast a tech.

streamer:wellness-brand::Charming Defens.text: Beginning at 10th level, your charm (both innate and augmented) makes you a hard sell. You are immune to being charmed, and when another creature attempts to charm you, you can use your reaction to attempt to turn the charm back on that creature. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your streamer tech save DC or be charmed by you for 1 minute or until the creature takes any damage.

streamer:wellness-brand::World of FOMO.text: Starting at 14th level, you can plunge a creature into a fog of indecision and doubt. As an action, choose a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you. It must make a Wisdom saving throw against your streamer tech save DC. On a failed save, it is charmed or frightened by you (your choice) for 1 minute or until your concentration is broken (as if you are concentrating on a tech). This effect ends early if the creature takes any damage.

streetfighter::Street Tough.text: Beginning at 1st level, while you are no armor and not wielding a shield, your AC equals 13 + your Constitution modifier. While you are wearing light armor, you use your Constitution instead of Dexterity to determine your additional AC.

streetfighter::These Hands.text: Beginning at 1st level, your years of fighting in back alleys, bars and the streets have given you mastery over combat styles that use unarmed strikes and street fighter weapons, which are simple melee weapons without the two-handed property, whips, and improvised weapons. You can’t use the finesse property of a weapon while using it as a street fighter weapon.

streetfighter::Mettle.text: Beginning at 2nd level, your vast experience on the streets has helped you develop the mettle of a champion fighter. This is represented by a number of mettle points. Your street fighter level determines the maximum number of points you have, as shown in the Mettle Points column of the Street Fighter table.

streetfighter::Grin and Bear It.text: Beginning at 2nd level, whenever you are subject to an effect that both deals damage and has additional secondary effects on a failed save (such as the shockwave tech), you can willingly choose to fail the save. In doing so, you take damage as normal, regain one mettle point, and ignore all other secondary effects (such as forced movement, effects such as the frightened condition, etc.). You can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.

streetfighter::Just Getting Started.text: Beginning at 3rd level, when you take damage that reduces you to half your maximum hit points or less, you can use your reaction to gain temporary hit points equal to three times your street fighter level and regain all your expended mettle points. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

streetfighter::Fighting Discipline.text: Beginning at 3rd level, you choose a discipline that best exemplifies your style. Your discipline grants you features at 3rd level and again at 6th, 11th, and 17th level.

streetfighter::Ability Score Improvement.text: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can't increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

streetfighter::Fight or Flight.text: Beginning at 4th level, you discover a strength inside you that can’t be broken. As a bonus action, you gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage for one minute. At the end of that minute, you gain a level of physical exhaustion, or fatigue.

streetfighter::Extra Attack.text: Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

streetfighter::Downright Fierce.text: Beginning at 5th level, when you make an attack, you can declare you are taking a big swing. When you do, you have disadvantage on the attack roll and, if you hit with a street fighter weapon or unarmed strike, you deal the maximum result of your weapon’s damage die instead of rolling.

streetfighter::Power of Mettle.text: Beginning at 6th level, your unarmed strikes count as technical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to non-technical attacks and damage.

streetfighter::Footsies.text: At 7th level, you gain proficiency in Dexterity saving throws.

streetfighter::Snap Out of It.text: Beginning at 7th level, you can use your action to end one effect on yourself that is causing you to be charmed or frightened.

streetfighter::Momentum Shift.text: Beginning at 9th level, when you use your Just Getting Started feature, you can choose to also use this feature. If you do, you add your proficiency bonus to the damage of your unarmed strikes and street fighter weapons for the next minute.

streetfighter::Keep It Together.text: By 10th level, you have developed a natural knack for staying awake and standing in many situations where others would go down. You have resistance to software damage and have advantage on saving throws against effects that would make you stunned or unconscious.

streetfighter::Unbreakable.text: Starting at 14th level, you gain advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws. Additionally, whenever you make a saving throw and fail, you can spend 1 mettle point to reroll it and take the second result.

streetfighter::Tireless Athleticism.text: Starting at 15th level, your carrying capacity is doubled, and when you deal damage with a melee weapon or unarmed strike to an inanimate object, that damage is doubled. Your standing jump distance is the same as your running start jump distance.

streetfighter::Get Back Up.text: Starting at 18th level, when you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can find a well of strength within you to draw from against all odds. When you do, you regain half of your maximum hit points, half of your maximum mettle points, and do not suffer the effects of any levels of exhaustion you have for the next 10 minutes. At the end of those 10 minutes, you gain a level of exhaustion. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

streetfighter::Master of the Streets.text: At 20th level, your Strength and Constitution ability scores increase by 2, and your Strength and Constitution maximum ability scores also increase by 2. Additionally, when you take a long rest, you recover 2 levels of exhaustion instead of 1 and you regain all your expended Hit Dice instead of only half.

streetfighter:bare-knuckle::Burning Knuc.text: Starting when you choose this discipline at 3rd level, your unarmed strikes score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

streetfighter:bare-knuckle::Turn Around.text: Also starting at 3rd level, you can slip past the brunt of an attack and launch one of your own in the same fluid motion. When you take damage from a melee weapon attack, you can use your reaction and spend 2 mettle points to reduce the damage by 1d10 + your Strength modifier + your pugilist level.

streetfighter:bare-knuckle::Hard Knockdo.text: Starting at 6th level, when you use your bonus action to use the Basic Combination and hit the same creature with both attacks, you can spend 1 mettle point to make an additional unarmed strike against that creature as part of the same bonus action. If you hit, the creature is knocked prone in addition to taking damage as normal for your unarmed strike.

streetfighter:bare-knuckle::Jolt Counter.text: Starting at 11th level, when you reduce damage from an attack to 0 and successfully hit an enemy creature using your Turn Around Punch feature, you regain 1 expended mettle point.

streetfighter:bare-knuckle::Gigaton Uppe.text: Starting at 17th level, when you hit with an unarmed strike or street fighter weapon, you can spend 1 or more mettle points to try to knock out the opponent instead of dealing damage. Roll 3d12, plus an additional 2d12 for every mettle point spent after the first, and add your street fighter level to the result. If the total is equal to or greater than the creature’s remaining hit points, it is reduced to 0 hit points.

streetfighter:catch-wrestler::Grappling.text: Starting when you choose this discipline at 3rd level, you gain the following additional mettle features.

streetfighter:catch-wrestler::Jacked.text: Also at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in Athletics if you don’t already have it. If you do already have proficiency in Athletics, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check that uses that proficiency.

streetfighter:catch-wrestler::Entangled.text: Starting at 6th level, when you have an enemy creature grappled, you gain half cover against all attacks made against you by a creature you are not grappling. When a weapon attack made by a creature you are not grappling misses you, you can use your reaction and spend 1 mettle point to have that creature make the same attack with a new roll against an enemy creature you are grappling.

streetfighter:catch-wrestler::Larger Tha.text: Starting at 11th level, you count as being one size larger for the purposes of grappling and shoving. In addition, you can move your full movement speed when you are dragging or carrying a grappled creature your size or smaller.

streetfighter:catch-wrestler::Ground and.text: At 17th level, your mastery of grappling reaches its peak. While you have a creature grappled, you gain advantage on all attacks against it. Additionally, when you make an unarmed strike or streetfighter weapon attack against a creature you have grappled, you score a critical hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

streetfighter:dirty-dog::Bonus Proficien.text: When you choose this discipline at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Intimidation skill if you don’t have it already. If you do, you gain proficiency in your choice of the Deception or Sleight of Hand skill.

streetfighter:dirty-dog::Boisterous Taun.text: Also at 3rd level, you become a master at pissing people off. You can use a bonus action on your turn to provoke a creature within 60 feet who can see or hear you. That creature must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the creature takes software damage equal to a roll of your hands die + your Charisma modifier and has disadvantage on any attack rolls it makes that do not include you as a target before the start of your next turn.

streetfighter:dirty-dog::Dirty Deeds.text: Starting at 6th level, you know a few things that help you even the odds when the going gets rough. You can use each of these tricks once and regain their use when you finish a short or long rest.

streetfighter:dirty-dog::Grating Words.text: Starting at 11th level, your threats and dirty deeds pack an extra punch. When you make a Charisma (Intimidation) check, you can use your reaction and spend 1 mettle to give yourself advantage on the roll. When a creature makes a saving throw against one of your Dirty Dog features, you can use your reaction and spend 1 mettle to give that roll disadvantage.

streetfighter:dirty-dog::Loudmouthed.text: Starting at 17th level, you gain the ability to piss every creature in the room off with minimal effort. When you use your Boisterous Taunt feature, you can choose to target a number of creatures within 60 feet who can see or hear you up to your level in this class, instead of a single creature. You regain 1 expended mettle point the first time each of these targets hits you with an attack before the start of your next turn. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

streetfighter:lucha-libre::Bonus Profici.text: When you choose this discipline at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Performance skill, if you don’t have it already. If you do, you gain proficiency in your choice of the Intimidation or Persuasion skill.

streetfighter:lucha-libre::Kayfabe.text: Also at 3rd level, you create an alternate persona that you can adopt or discard as a bonus action on your turn. When you create an alternate persona, you should give the persona a striking name as well as some physical signifier (such as a mask, colorful cape, or another prominent idiosyncratic feature). Unless you tell a creature, or the creature sees you adopt your persona, they do not know you and the adopted persona are the same person.

streetfighter:lucha-libre::Work the Crow.text: Starting at 6th level, while you have adopted your alternate persona, you can use your action to inspire your choice of fear or adoration in those nearby. When you do, creatures of your choice within 30 feet who can see you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier) or be charmed if you chose adoration, or frightened if you chose fear. This effect lasts for one minute. Each time a creature takes damage from you or one of your allies, it can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on a success.

streetfighter:lucha-libre::High Flying W.text: Starting at 11th level, your base walking speed increases by 10 feet, your jump distances are doubled, and you can use a bonus action on each of your turns to take the Dash action. Additionally, all falling damage you take is halved.

streetfighter:lucha-libre::Finisher.text: Starting at 17th level, you create a finisher that you can use while you have adopted your alternate persona. Give your finisher a name and a description. You can replace one of your attacks on your turn with this finisher.

streetfighter:pact-bouncer::\"Donated\".text: When you choose this discipline at 3rd level, you learn the charged railgun shot and nanotech twiddling tricks. Constitution is your techcasting ability for these techs, since your oh-so-generous benefactors petered out your gift through dubiously hidden nanite infusions and hardlight exposure.

streetfighter:pact-bouncer::The Beat Sti.text: Also starting at 3rd level, you can use a bonus action on your turn to purge your body of excessive PACT-branded nano or holo tech. When you do, one of your limbs (often an arm) is technologically overlayed with a brand-appropriate yet intimidating translucent visage of power for 1 minute (a tentacle for HentaiHub, a dark claw for Goth Topic, etc.), granting you the following benefits:

streetfighter:pact-bouncer::PACT Rewards.text: Starting at 6th level, you gain two sponsorship programs of your choice from among those available to the streamer class. For every two levels you have in this class, you count as possessing one streamer, as if you were a streamer, for the purpose of meeting a sponsorship program or feat's prerequisites. Constitution is your techcasting ability for any techs you gain as a result of one of these sponsorship programs, and any sponsorship program gained this way that references your Charisma modifier uses your Strength modifier instead.

streetfighter:pact-bouncer::The Hired Mu.text: Starting at 11th level, when you use the beat stick feature, you can choose to encase yourself entirely, growing into a real billboard of a blockade for an equal amount of time. When you do, your size increases by one category—from Medium to Large, for example—if there is enough room to support such growth. Regardless of if you change sizes, while this feature is active, you have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, your reach becomes 10 feet, and your melee weapon attacks deal 1d4 extra damage.

streetfighter:pact-bouncer::Use of Exces.text: Starting at 17th level, you can use an action and expend 6 mettle points to attempt to escort a rowdy customer outside of the establishment of life, utilizing your "gifts" to burrow your hand into one target creature within your reach's body and extracting its innards. The creature must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier). On a failure, the creature takes 100 technical piercing damage. On a success, the creature takes 50 technical piercing damage instead.

streetfighter:street-detective::Back All.text: When you choose this discipline at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with two of the following skills of your choice: Insight, Investigation, or Perception. In addition, when you make an Intelligence (Investigation), Wisdom (Insight), or Wisdom (Perception) check, you can spend 1 mettle point to gain advantage on the check.

streetfighter:street-detective::Hypervig.text: Also starting at 3rd level, you have advantage on initiative rolls. During the first round of combat, you have advantage on attack rolls against creatures who haven’t acted yet.

streetfighter:street-detective::Analytic.text: Starting at 6th level, you can use a bonus action and expend 2 mettle points to hone in on the idiosyncrasies and bad habits of an enemy you can see within 30 feet.

streetfighter:street-detective::Pulse of.text: Starting at 11th level, when you take a long rest in a specific district of Neon City, or a settlement outside of it, you can choose to become familiar with the location. When you use this feature again, you replace your previous familiar location with the current one. You gain the following benefits while in a familiar location:

streetfighter:street-detective::Unerring.text: Starting at 17th level, you can use a bonus action and spend 1 mettle point to open your senses to your surroundings for 1 minute. During this time, you have advantage on saving throws against being blinded or deafened and have truesight out to a distance of 30 feet.

techwizard::Techcasting.text: As a student of reality-warping technology, you have a cyberdeck containing techs that show the first glimmerings of your true power.

techwizard::Learning Techs of 1st Level.text: Each time you gain a techwizard level, you can add two techwizard techs of your choice Techwizard tech list to your cyberdeck. Each of these techs must be of a level for which you have tech slots, as shown on the Techwizard table. On your adventures, you might find other techs that you can add to your cyberdeck.

techwizard::Memory Cache.text: You have learned to refresh some of your techs by studying your cyberdeck. Once per day when you finish a short rest, you can choose expended tech slots to recover. The tech slots can have a combined level that is equal to or less than half your techwizard level (rounded up), and none of the slots can be 6th level or higher.

techwizard::Tech Specialty.text: Though all techwizards are highly proficient with the use of modern technology, each of them eventually develops an affinity for a particular sort of technical application. These tech specialties reflect the sort of highly specialized training necessary to master the most potent forms of tech, as well as unique methods of utilizing common techs in highly divergent ways.

techwizard::Trick Formulas.text: At 3rd level, you have formulated a universal theory that allows you to rapidly alter your knowledge of tech-based tricks. Whenever you finish a long rest and consult those formulas in your cyberdeck, you can replace one techwizard trick you know with another trick from the techwizard tech list.

techwizard::Ability Score Improvement.text: When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.

techwizard::Tech Mastery.text: At 18th level, you have achieved such mastery over certain techs that you can cast them at will. Choose a 1st-level techwizard tech and a 2nd-level techwizard tech that are in your cyberdeck. You can cast those techs at their lowest level without expending a tech slot when you have them prepared. If you want to cast either tech at a higher level, you must expend a tech slot as normal.

techwizard::Signature Techs.text: When you reach 20th level, you gain mastery over two powerful techs and can cast them with little effort. Choose two 3rd-level techwizard techs in your cyberdeck as your signature techs. You always have these techs prepared, they don’t count against the number of techs you have prepared, and you can cast each of them once at 3rd level without expending a tech slot. When you do so, you can’t do so again until you finish a short or long rest.

techwizard:bulwark::Absolute Terror Fiel.text: At 2nd level, you have learned to generate a powerful force field to fortify yourself against harm. When you are hit by an attack or you fail a saving throw, you can use your reaction to gain a +2 bonus to your AC against that attack or a +4 bonus to that saving throw.

techwizard:bulwark::Tactical Wit.text: Starting at 2nd level, your keen ability to assess tactical situations allows you to act quickly in battle. You gain a bonus on initiative rolls equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 0).

techwizard:bulwark::Power Surge.text: Starting at 6th level, you can store discharged tech energy in your peripherals to later empower your damaging techs.

techwizard:bulwark::Durable Magic.text: Beginning at 10th level, the energy you channel helps ward off harm. While you maintain concentration on a tech, you have a +2 bonus to AC and all saving throws.

techwizard:bulwark::Deflection Field.text: At 14th level, your Absolute Terror Field becomes infused with deadly energy. When you use your Absolute Terror Field feature, you can cause kinetic energy to arc from you. Up to three creatures of your choice within 60 feet of you each take kinetic damage equal to half your techwizard level.

techwizard:code-monkey::Conception Exper.text: Beginning when you select this school at 2nd level, the cash and time you must spend to copy a Conception tech into your cyberdeck is halved.

techwizard:code-monkey::Neuro-Linguistic.text: Starting at 2nd level when you choose this specialty, your soft words and carefully controlled micro-expressions can enthrall another creature. As an action, choose one creature that you can see within 5 feet of you. If the target can see or hear you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your techwizard tech save DC or be charmed by you until the end of your next turn. The charmed creature’s speed drops to 0, and the creature is incapacitated and visibly dazed.

techwizard:code-monkey::Meta-Model Defle.text: Beginning at 6th level, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to divert the attack, provided that another creature is within the attack’s range. The attacker must make a Wisdom saving throw against your techwizard tech save DC. On a failed save, the attacker must target the creature that is closest to it, not including you or itself. If multiple creatures are closest, the attacker chooses which one to target.

techwizard:code-monkey::Dual-Core Proces.text: Starting at 10th level, when you cast a Conception tech of 1st level or higher that targets only one creature, you can have it target a second creature.

techwizard:code-monkey::Brain Hacking.text: At 14th level, you gain the ability to make a creature unaware of your neural influence on it. When you cast a Conception tech to charm one or more creatures, you can alter one creature’s understanding so that it remains unaware of being charmed.

techwizard:fabricator::Manifestation Exp.text: Beginning when you select this specialty at 2nd level, the cash and time you must spend to copy a Manifestation tech into your cyberdeck is halved.

techwizard:fabricator::Minor Fabrication.text: Starting at 2nd level when you select this specialty, you can use your action to create an inanimate object in your hand or on the ground in an unoccupied space that you can see within 10 feet of you. This object can be no larger than 3 feet on a side and weigh no more than 10 pounds, and its form must be that of a mundane object that you have seen. The object is visibly cobbled-together, made from spare parts, junk, and 3D-printed components.

techwizard:fabricator::Expedited Shippin.text: Starting at 6th level, you can use your action to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space that you can see. Alternatively, you can choose a space within range that is occupied by a Small or Medium creature. If that creature is willing, you both teleport, swapping places.

techwizard:fabricator::Focused Manifesta.text: Beginning at 10th level, while you are concentrating on a Manifestation tech, your concentration can’t be broken as a result of taking damage.

techwizard:fabricator::Durable Fabricati.text: Starting at 14th level, any creature or object that you summon or create with a Manifestation tech has 30 temporary hit points.

techwizard:insurance-adjustor::Protectio.text: Beginning when you select this specialty at 2nd level, the cash and time you must spend to copy a Protection tech into your cyberdeck is halved.

techwizard:insurance-adjustor::Tech Ward.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can weave a dense energy field around yourself for protection. When you cast a Protection tech of 1st level or higher, you can simultaneously use some of the tech’s power to create a force field on yourself that lasts until you finish a long rest. The ward has hit points equal to twice your techwizard level + your Intelligence modifier. Whenever you take damage, the ward takes the damage instead. If this damage reduces the ward to 0 hit points, you take any remaining damage.

techwizard:insurance-adjustor::Projected.text: Starting at 6th level, when a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can use your reaction to cause your Tech Ward to absorb that damage. If this damage reduces the ward to 0 hit points, the warded creature takes any remaining damage.

techwizard:insurance-adjustor::Skillful.text: Beginning at 10th level, when you cast a Protection tech that requires you to make an ability check as a part of casting that tech (as in localized EMP or counter EMP burst), you add your proficiency bonus to that ability check.

techwizard:insurance-adjustor::Tech Resi.text: Starting at 14th level, you have advantage on saving throws against techs. Furthermore, you have resistance against the damage of techs.

techwizard:it-generalist::Custom Hardwar.text: At 2nd level, choose 1 tech that you know to set-up periphery hardware for. This tech is always prepared and does not count against your total number of techs known or prepared. You select an additional tech to set-up at 6th, 10th, and 14th level.

techwizard:it-generalist::Retrostyle Cyb.text: Cobbled together from all your favorite end user computational aids from the last century, you've put together a highly personal cyberdeck. At 2nd level, while you are holding the deck, it grants you the following benefits:

techwizard:it-generalist::Custom Burner.text: At 6th level, you can cast a tech within an electronic device of your choosing, one with the processing power of at least a burner phone, selecting any options for the tech at the time of casting, but the tech does not take effect and is instead programmed into the burner. The burner can be activated as if casting the tech. Alternatively, you can expend the burner along with a tech slot of the same level as the programmed tech to cast a prepared tech of one level higher.

techwizard:it-generalist::Remote Casting.text: At 10th level, you can cast techs through networked devices, such as cameras, mobile phones, and computers. You can only remote cast techs that target specific creatures, and must be able to see or otherwise determine the position of such targets. If the tech requires the caster to be seen or heard, the target must see you, hear you, or a live feed of you, as required. The tech's range is determined using the distance from you to your device, and then from the target to its device.

techwizard:it-generalist::Off and On Aga.text: By 14th level, you can create and maintain up to three custom burner's per long rest. You've long since learned that the simplest solution to a problem is often the most direct; foresight, backups, restart. When a tech you cast would be prematurely ended, such as by losing concentration, or being targeted by Localized EMP or Counter EMP, you can instead, as a reaction, choose to maintain your focus and the tech by expending a custom burner that contains a tech of equal or greater level.

techwizard:marketing-campaigner::Decepti.text: Beginning when you select this specialty at 2nd level, the cash and time you must spend to copy an Deception tech into your cyberdeck is halved.

techwizard:marketing-campaigner::Hardlig.text: When you choose this specialty at 2nd level, you learn the hardlight chicanery trick. If you already know this trick, you learn a different techwizard trick of your choice. The trick doesn’t count against your number of tricks known.

techwizard:marketing-campaigner::Malleab.text: Starting at 6th level, when you cast an Deception tech that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can use your action to change the nature of the projection (using the tech’s normal parameters for the projection), provided that you can see the projection.

techwizard:marketing-campaigner::Hologra.text: Beginning at 10th level, you can create an illusory duplicate of yourself as an instant, almost instinctual reaction to danger. When a creature makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to interpose the hologram duplicate between the attacker and yourself. The attack automatically misses you, then the illusion dissipates.

techwizard:marketing-campaigner::Virtual.text: By 14th level, you have learned how to use hardlight projections and force fields to give your illusory projects a semblance of reality. When you cast an Deception tech of 1st level or higher, you can choose one inanimate mundane object that is part of the illusion and make that object real. You can do this on your turn as a bonus action while the tech is ongoing. The object remains real for 1 minute. For example, you can create a hologram of a bridge over a chasm and then make it real long enough for your allies to cross.

techwizard:master-blaster::Altercation E.text: Beginning when you select this specialty at 2nd level, the cash and time you must spend to copy an Altercation tech into your cyberdeck is halved.

techwizard:master-blaster::Friendly Fire.text: Beginning at 2nd level, you can create pockets of relative safety within the effects of your Altercation techs. When you cast a Altercation tech that affects other creatures that you can see, you can choose a number of them equal to 1 + the tech’s level. The chosen creatures automatically succeed on their saving throws against the tech, and they take no damage if they would normally take half damage on a successful save.

techwizard:master-blaster::Potent Trick.text: Starting at 6th level, your damaging tricks affect even creatures that avoid the brunt of the effect. When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against your trick, the creature takes half the trick’s damage (if any) but suffers no additional effect from the trick.

techwizard:master-blaster::Empowered Tec.text: Beginning at 10th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage roll of any techwizard Altercation tech that you cast. The damage bonus applies to one damage roll of a tech, not multiple rolls.

techwizard:master-blaster::Overchannel.text: Starting at 14th level, you can increase the power of your simpler techs. When you cast a techwizard tech of 5th level or lower that deals damage and isn’t a trick, you can deal maximum damage with that tech.

techwizard:nanotechnician::Manipulation.text: Beginning when you select this specialty at 2nd level, the cash and time you must spend to copy a Manipulation tech into your cyberdeck is halved.

techwizard:nanotechnician::Matter Rearra.text: Starting at 2nd level when you select this specialty, you can temporarily alter the physical properties of one mundane object, changing it from one substance into another. You use your slaved nanites on one object composed entirely of wood, stone, plastic, or metal, transforming it into a different one of those materials. The material generated cannot be more valuable than the base material—only different.

techwizard:nanotechnician::Nanotech Infu.text: Starting at 6th level, you can spend 8 hours creating an infusion of nanites. You can benefit from the infusion yourself or slave it to another creature. A creature gains a benefit of your choice as long as the infusion is in the creature’s possession. When you create the infusion, choose the benefit from the following options:

techwizard:nanotechnician::Personal Refo.text: At 10th level, you add the reformat tech to your cyberdeck, if it is not there already. You can cast reformat without expending a tech slot. When you do so, you can target only yourself and transform into a beast whose challenge rating is 1 or lower.

techwizard:nanotechnician::Nanite Swarm.text: Starting at 14th level, you can use your action to consume the reserve of energy stored within your nanotech infusion in a single burst. When you do so, choose one of the following effects. Your nanotech infusion is destroyed and can’t be remade until you finish a long rest.

techwizard:nexus-modder::Hardlight Stylu.text: At 2nd level, as a bonus action, you can create a stylus made of hardlight in your free hand. The hardlight stylus has the following properties:

techwizard:nexus-modder::Awakened Cyberd.text: Using fragments of code and your own mad hacking, you have awakened a synthetic intelligence within your cyberdeck.

techwizard:nexus-modder::Manifest Mind.text: At 6th level, you can conjure forth the mind of your Awakened Cyberdeck. As a bonus action while the deck is on your person, you can cause the mind to manifest as a Tiny hardlight hologram, hovering in an unoccupied space of your choice within 60 feet of you. The mind is intangible and doesn’t occupy its space, and it sheds dim light in a 10-foot radius. It has an appearance of your choice, chosen the first time you use this ability.

techwizard:nexus-modder::Master Coder.text: At 10th level, whenever you finish a long rest, you can create one burner by touching your Hardlight Stylus to a blank burner and causing one tech from your Awakened Cyberdeck to be copied onto the tablet. The cyberdeck must be within 5 feet of you when you make the burner.

techwizard:nexus-modder::One with the Co.text: At 14th level, your connection to your Awakened Cyberdeck has become so profound that your mind has become entwined with it. While the deck is on your person, you have advantage on all Intelligence (Technology) checks, as the cyberdeck helps you remember important technical data.

techwizard:sentai-savior::Dramatic Comba.text: When you adopt this specialty at 2nd level, you gain proficiency with light armor, and you gain proficiency with one type of one-handed melee weapon of your choice.

techwizard:sentai-savior::Henshin Transf.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your techs to briefly augment yourself to superhuman levels, provided that you aren’t wearing medium or heavy armor or using a shield. This transformation gives you preternatural speed, agility, and focus.

techwizard:sentai-savior::Extra Attack.text: Starting at 6th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast one of your tricks in place of one of those attacks.

techwizard:sentai-savior::Spark Defense.text: Beginning at 10th level, you can direct your tech to absorb damage while your Henshin Transformation is active, releasing sparks instead of blood when you would be wounded. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to expend one tech slot and reduce that damage to you by an amount equal to five times the tech slot’s level (to a minimum of 0).

techwizard:sentai-savior::Sentai Strike!.text: Starting at 14th level, you can add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the damage of your melee weapon attacks while your Henshin Transformation is active.

techwizard:singularity-technician::Singu.text: You can learn techs from the Quantum Theory and Singularity sub-specialties normally.

techwizard:singularity-technician::Adjus.text: At 2nd level, as an action, you can use your tech to alter the weight of one object or creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The object or creature must be Large or smaller. The target’s weight is halved or doubled for up to 1 minute or until your concentration ends (as if you were concentrating on a tech).

techwizard:singularity-technician::Gravi.text: When you reach 6th level, whenever you cast a tech on a creature, you can move the target 5 feet to an unoccupied space of your choice if the target is willing to move, the tech hits it with an attack, or it fails a saving throw against the tech.

techwizard:singularity-technician::Viole.text: At 10th level, when another creature that you can see within 60 feet of you hits with a weapon attack, you can use your reaction to increase the attack’s velocity, causing the attack’s target to take an extra 1d10 damage of the weapon’s type.

techwizard:singularity-technician::Event.text: Starting at 14th level, as an action, you can generate a powerful field of gravitational energy that tugs at other creatures for up to 1 minute or until your concentration ends (as if you were concentrating on a tech). For the duration, whenever a creature hostile to you starts its turn within 30 feet of you, it must make a Strength saving throw against your tech save DC. On a failed save, it takes 2d10 kinetic damage, and its speed is reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage, and every foot it moves this turn costs 2 extra feet of movement.

techwizard:stasis-technician::Stasis Spe.text: You can learn techs from the Quantum Theory and Stasis sub-specialties normally.

techwizard:stasis-technician::Chronal Sh.text: At 2nd level, you can exert limited control over the flow of time around a creature. As a reaction, after you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can force the creature to reroll. You make this decision after you see whether the roll succeeds or fails. The target must use the result of the second roll.

techwizard:stasis-technician::Temporal A.text: Starting at 2nd level, you can add your Intelligence modifier (minimum 0) to your initiative rolls.

techwizard:stasis-technician::Momentary.text: When you reach 6th level, as an action, you can force a Large or smaller creature you can see within 60 feet of you to make a Constitution saving throw against your tech save DC. Unless the saving throw is a success, the creature is encased in a field of chronal energy until the end of your next turn or until the creature takes any damage. While encased in this way, the creature is incapacitated and has a speed of 0.

techwizard:stasis-technician::Tech Abeya.text: At 10th level, when you cast a tech using a tech slot of 4th level or lower, you can condense the tech’s power into a stasis mote. The tech is frozen in time at the moment of casting and held within a gray stasis field for 1 hour. This mote is a Tiny object with AC 15 and 1 hit point, and it is immune to poison and software damage. When the duration ends, or if the mote is destroyed, it vanishes in a flash of light, and the tech is lost.

techwizard:stasis-technician::Convergent.text: Starting at 14th level, you can peer through possible futures and pull one of them into events around you, ensuring a particular outcome. When you or a creature you can see within 60 feet of you makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction to ignore the die roll and decide whether the number rolled is the minimum needed to succeed or one less than that number (your choice).

techwizard:surveillance-specialist::Obse.text: Beginning when you select this specialty at 2nd level, the cash and time you must spend to copy a Observation tech into your cyberdeck is halved.

techwizard:surveillance-specialist::Pred.text: Starting at 2nd level when you choose this specialty, your peripherals are constantly running predictions for possible outcomes. When you finish a long rest, roll two d20s and record the numbers rolled. You can replace any attack roll, saving throw, or ability check made by you or a creature that you can see with one of these predictive rolls. You must choose to do so before the roll, and you can replace a roll in this way only once per turn.

techwizard:surveillance-specialist::Expe.text: Beginning at 6th level, casting Observation techs comes so easily to you that it expends only a fraction of your efforts. When you cast a Observation tech of 2nd level or higher using a tech slot, you regain one expended tech slot. The slot you regain must be of a level lower than the tech you cast and can’t be higher than 5th level.

techwizard:surveillance-specialist::Sens.text: Starting at 10th level, you can use your action to increase your powers of perception. When you do so, choose one of the following benefits, which lasts until you are incapacitated or you take a short or long rest. You can’t use the feature again until you finish a short or long rest.

techwizard:surveillance-specialist::Well.text: Starting at 14th level, your predictive algorithms become significantly more accurate. You roll three d20s for your Predictive Algorithm feature, rather than two.

techwizard:technomancer::Biochemistry Ex.text: Beginning when you select this specialty at 2nd level, the cash and time you must spend to copy a Biochemistry tech into your cyberdeck is halved.

techwizard:technomancer::Orgone Harvest.text: At 2nd level, you gain the ability to reap leftover bio-energy from creatures you kill with your techs. Once per turn when you kill one or more creatures with a tech of 1st level or higher, you regain hit points equal to twice the tech’s level, or three times its level if the tech belongs to the Biochemistry specialty. You don’t gain this benefit for killing machines or hacked.

techwizard:technomancer::Hacked Thralls.text: At 6th level, you add the activate husk tech to your cyberdeck if it is not there already. When you cast activate husk, you can target one additional corpse, creating another tech husk or hollow chassis, as appropriate.

techwizard:technomancer::Entropic Shield.text: Beginning at 10th level, you have resistance to entropic damage, and your hit point maximum can’t be reduced. Your grasp of Biochemistry technology prevents your own health from withering.

techwizard:technomancer::Command Overrid.text: Starting at 14th level, you can use your tech to bring hacked under your control, even those you did not create. As an action, you can choose one hacked that you can see within 60 feet of you. That creature must make a Charisma saving throw against your techwizard tech save DC. If it succeeds, you can’t use this feature on it again. If it fails, it becomes friendly to you and obeys your commands until you use this feature again.
